requirement: Create a new private repository with no public fork relationship.
acceptance: Repository visibility tests confirm access is restricted to approved organisation members.
notes: The authoritative checkout is local/bundle-backed and the connected GitHub installation exposes no matching hosted campaign-platform repository. Private visibility and approved-organisation-member access therefore cannot yet be evidenced.

requirement: Retain the OpenWA MIT licence and original notices.
acceptance: Licence and NOTICE/UPSTREAM files are present in every release artefact.
notes: The repository retains the proprietary root notice, OpenWA third-party notice, provenance record and original MIT licence in the vendored source. No automated release-artifact packaging/verification step was found that proves these files are present in every release artefact, so the exact acceptance remains open.

requirement: Record the exact imported upstream URL, commit SHA and import date.
acceptance: UPSTREAM.md and build metadata identify the baseline.
notes: The exact upstream URL, supplied archive name/version, archive SHA-256 and import/review date are recorded. The imported archive has no .git metadata and the exact upstream Git commit is explicitly UNVERIFIED, so the required commit SHA/build-baseline identity is incomplete.

requirement: Configure upstream as read-only reference only.
acceptance: No automated push or merge path exists from upstream.
notes: Policy explicitly treats public OpenWA upstream as read-only, untrusted input and prohibits automatic merge/deployment; the checkout has no public-upstream Git remote and CI has no upstream fetch/merge job. This is documented/structural evidence rather than an enforced hosted remote policy, so the row remains partial.

requirement: Fetch upstream changes into an isolated review branch.
acceptance: Changes cannot reach main without internal pull request and required checks.
notes: The documented update model requires manual import into an isolated review branch followed by provenance/security review, tests and internal review, and CI runs on pull requests. No tracked upstream-fetch workflow or hosted branch-rule evidence proves an upstream update can only reach main through that controlled review path.

requirement: Disable or restrict private repository forking.
acceptance: Organisation and repository policy evidence exists.
notes: No matching hosted repository is visible through the connected GitHub installation, so organisation/repository fork restrictions cannot be evidenced from either the checkout or hosted settings.

requirement: Protect main and release branches.
acceptance: Direct push, force push and unreviewed merge are blocked.
notes: CI exists for pull requests and main pushes, but branch-protection rules blocking direct/force push and unreviewed merges are hosted repository settings and no matching hosted repository is available to verify them.

requirement: Require code-owner approval for gateway, security, database and infrastructure changes.
acceptance: A test pull request demonstrates enforcement.
notes: No CODEOWNERS file is committed and no hosted test pull request/required code-owner rule is available to demonstrate enforced approval for gateway, security, database and infrastructure changes.

requirement: Pin dependencies and container images.
acceptance: Lockfiles and immutable image references are committed.
notes: Deployed Node applications have lockfiles and production Compose requires image values to be digest-pinned at deployment. The root package has no package-lock.json, production image digests are supplied externally rather than committed, CI actions use floating major tags, and strict SBOM verification currently fails on the missing root lockfile.

requirement: Generate a software bill of materials for releases.
acceptance: Release pipeline produces and retains an SBOM.
notes: A deterministic CycloneDX generator exists and the normal release-security gate freshly produced a 30-component SBOM. CI invokes that gate, but the workflow does not upload/retain the generated SBOM as a release artefact and artifacts/sbom.cdx.json is not tracked, so release retention is not proven.

requirement: Scan source, dependencies, secrets and images.
acceptance: CI fails for configured critical findings unless an approved exception exists.
notes: Fresh normal release-security validation passed production-compose structure, committed-secret scanning and npm dependency audits with no production exceptions. gitleaks/Trivy/Syft are available only behind STRICT_RELEASE_SECURITY and normal CI does not enable that mode or perform a release image vulnerability scan, so the full source/dependency/secret/image gate is incomplete.

requirement: Do not automatically deploy upstream or dependency updates.
acceptance: All updates require review, tests and staging approval.
notes: The repository contains no first-party Dependabot/Renovate/upstream auto-merge or deployment workflow; upstream policy explicitly requires manual review and CI checks. Hosted required-review and staging-approval enforcement is not evidenced, so the exact all-updates acceptance remains partial.

requirement: Expose a versioned internal provider API independent of the OpenWA public API.
acceptance: Contract tests pass against the provider interface.
notes: The consolidated worker exposes a versioned /v1 internal contract over MessagingProvider rather than the upstream OpenWA public API. OpenWAProvider delegates that contract directly to the embedded engine, and the embedded provider/lifecycle contract test plus the production Docker build verify the interface.

requirement: Require an idempotency key for every delivery command.
acceptance: Duplicate command returns the original outcome and does not perform another send.
notes: Every send requires a validated idempotency key. Durable pre-submit evidence survives restart; concurrent/replayed duplicates return the original provider outcome without another provider call, while unresolved or UNKNOWN outcomes are never submitted again automatically.

requirement: Own each live session on exactly one worker node.
acceptance: Lease/ownership tests prevent concurrent activation.
notes: A PostgreSQL concurrency test proves only one worker acquires a live session lease and stale ownership is fenced after takeover. The gateway separately persists and validates session authority so stale/conflicting owners are rejected before provider send.

requirement: Persist session state on an encrypted worker volume.
acceptance: Restart test restores authorised sessions without re-pairing where provider permits.
notes: Engine authentication/session directories are wired to persistent worker storage, but the acceptance truth requires an encrypted production worker volume and a genuine authenticated WhatsApp restart proving restoration without re-pairing where the engine permits. That Hostinger/live-provider evidence is not yet available.

requirement: Report heartbeat, build version, capacity, queue depth and resource health.
acceptance: Control plane marks stale worker unavailable within configured threshold.
notes: Signed runtime registration reports heartbeat/build/runtime identity, capacity, session count, queue depth, CPU, memory, disk, inode, process/file-descriptor and network evidence. Fresh PostgreSQL acceptance proves the governed stale threshold marks only expired nodes unavailable.

requirement: Report session connection, authentication, last-success and failure state.
acceptance: Operations dashboard reflects forced disconnects and reconnections.
notes: The worker exposes connection/authentication lifecycle, connected/last-active timestamps and failure detail, while the control plane records heartbeat and canonical last-success evidence. There is not yet a proven signed per-session state propagation path showing forced gateway disconnect/reconnect transitions in the operations dashboard.

requirement: Accept work only for sessions currently leased to the worker.
acceptance: Cross-node assignment is rejected and audited.
notes: Dispatch persists a fenced session authority before sending and now appends an immutable REJECTED event when a stale/conflicting cross-node owner loses the authority upsert. PostgreSQL acceptance proves the live owner is unchanged and the rejection is audited; gateway fencing proves the rejected owner cannot reach provider send.

requirement: Use a bounded per-session pipeline and configurable in-flight limit.
acceptance: Load test proves the configured bound is enforced.
notes: Each session has its own bounded pipeline with configurable in-flight and waiter limits. A direct load acceptance runs 30 operations against one session with SESSION_IN_FLIGHT_LIMIT=3 and observes a maximum of exactly 3 concurrent operations with the queue draining to zero.

requirement: Support graceful drain before deployment or maintenance.
acceptance: No new jobs accepted; active jobs reach a recorded outcome.
notes: Governed node/session draining blocks new work while the gateway pipeline rejects queued/new operations after drain and lets already-active operations finish through their normal idempotent outcome path. Control-plane maintenance/drain state prevents unsafe new campaign/session work.

requirement: Return provider message identifiers and raw provider status metadata where safe.
acceptance: Delivery attempt record stores the identifier and redacted metadata.
notes: Provider message identifiers are returned by the gateway, carried on canonical events and persisted into recipient/attempt history. Provider status is normalised into canonical event/error fields; there is no separately persisted redacted raw-provider-status metadata object, so the exact metadata portion remains incomplete.

requirement: Forward inbound messages and delivery/read events through signed callbacks or a trusted event channel.
acceptance: Forged and replayed events are rejected.
notes: Delivery/read and inbound events are durably queued by the gateway and forwarded through signed callbacks. The control plane verifies signatures, replay windows and event identity; forged/replayed callbacks are rejected. Genuine WhatsApp callback shapes remain a separate live validation gate, not a reason to weaken this code-side acceptance.

requirement: Never store full campaign audience lists locally.
acceptance: Worker storage review confirms only bounded active-job data and session state.
notes: The worker has no campaign-audience repository. Durable send idempotency stores fingerprints/outcomes rather than recipient/body/route payloads and is capped; the acceptance test explicitly proves those raw send fields are absent from persisted idempotency evidence. Local outboxes contain individual transport events and session storage contains engine/session state, not audience lists.

requirement: Use object references for media and enforce size/type limits.
acceptance: Large media campaign does not hold the entire batch in memory.
notes: Messages freeze trusted object references, media type/size/checksum and route capability evidence. Dispatch resolves bounded object access per recipient and enforces the frozen provider attachment ceiling rather than materialising a campaign media batch in worker memory.

requirement: Sanitise logs and exclude raw MSISDN, message content and credentials by default.
acceptance: Automated log-content tests pass.
notes: The gateway uses a sanitising JSON logger and static-safe metrics. Automated durability/log tests prove raw MSISDN, QR/pairing material, session token, message content and credential-bearing DSN fragments are removed from logs/metrics.

requirement: Support safe shutdown and uncertain-state reporting.
acceptance: Kill-during-send test produces an UNKNOWN state rather than automatic duplicate resend.
notes: Shutdown hooks and durable outboxes preserve pending event work. A real child-process kill during provider submission now proves that restart converts crash-left PENDING submission evidence to UNKNOWN and the same idempotency key cannot automatically reach the provider again.

requirement: Expose engine capability and version.
acceptance: Control plane can block an incompatible campaign/message type.
notes: The control plane governs provider/engine capability and version definitions, freezes the exact binding into campaign/test-send evidence and blocks incompatible gateway, adapter, minimum-version or message-capability routes. The worker exposes its runtime identity/capabilities under the versioned internal API.

requirement: Support per-session stable proxy configuration where legitimately required.
acceptance: Configuration change is audited and connectivity tested.
notes: Per-session stable proxy configuration is encrypted/audited in PostgreSQL, requires privileged recent-MFA administration, cannot change while the session is active, and reaches both embedded engine shapes without persisting worker credentials. The remaining acceptance is an actual connectivity/egress test through the approved production proxy, which requires deployed Hostinger/network evidence.

requirement: Do not implement rapid IP rotation or enforcement-evasion behaviour.
acceptance: Security review confirms prohibited capabilities are absent.
notes: First-party proxy behavior is explicitly stable-session routing only: active-session changes are rejected, restart does not silently reuse prior proxy authority, and source review found no rotation scheduler, pool cycling or enforcement-evasion path. The approved runtime-governance design also explicitly prohibits rapid rotation/evasion.

requirement: Permit access only to provisioned internal users.
acceptance: Unprovisioned identities cannot authenticate.
notes: Fresh PostgreSQL acceptance proves an administrator-provisioned internal account can authenticate while an unprovisioned identity is rejected with invalid credentials; no self-registration path exists.

requirement: Support mandatory multi-factor authentication.
acceptance: Login without the second factor is rejected.
notes: MFA challenge/verification and persistent MFA sessions are directly proven, and provisioning/reset default to MFA. However account administration can set MFARequired=false and the login service permits first-factor-only sessions for such accounts, so the unconditional mandatory-MFA acceptance is not fully enforced.

requirement: Support configurable passwordless/SSO integration later without replacing domain authorisation.
acceptance: Identity provider can be swapped through configuration.
notes: No real pluggable OIDC/SAML/passwordless identity-provider abstraction/configuration was found; current authentication is internal password + TOTP.

requirement: Implement role-based access control with granular permissions.
acceptance: Permission matrix tests cover every protected action.
notes: Ordinary application routes are wrapped in RBAC permission middleware and targeted permission-denial tests exist, but there is no exhaustive permission-matrix acceptance covering every protected action with its exact expected permission.

requirement: Support users holding multiple roles with least-privilege union of permissions.
acceptance: Effective permissions are displayed and tested.
notes: Fresh PostgreSQL evidence proves one user can hold multiple roles and receives the least-privilege permission union (campaign.write + finance.write). The current /auth/me JSON deliberately omits the effective permissions map, so the acceptance-required display of effective permissions is incomplete.

requirement: Enforce maker-checker separation for campaign release.
acceptance: Campaign creator cannot perform final release when policy requires separation.
notes: Final campaign approval/release uses campaign.approve authorization plus four-eyes actor separation; creator/self-approver paths are rejected where maker-checker is required.

requirement: Require step-up authentication for exports, key changes, emergency overrides and destructive actions.
acceptance: Protected action prompts for fresh authentication.
notes: Fresh MFA step-up is enforced across exports, privacy/legal-hold actions, identity administration, platform-policy changes, campaign final approval/release, execution controls and destructive/import operations. A dedicated cryptographic-key-change/rotation action with step-up evidence is not implemented, so the full named scope is not closed.

requirement: Enforce configurable idle and absolute session expiry.
acceptance: Expired sessions cannot call APIs.
notes: Idle and absolute session timeouts are deployment-configurable, validated and wired into both memory and PostgreSQL runtimes; expired/revoked sessions are rejected by Authenticate before protected APIs execute.

requirement: Provide account disable, lock and credential reset.
acceptance: Disabled account loses access immediately.
notes: Fresh PostgreSQL acceptance proves administrator disable immediately revokes an existing live session and the revoked token cannot authenticate; credential reset and lock/unlock operations also revoke/reset access state.

requirement: Detect repeated failed login attempts and apply configurable controls.
acceptance: Threshold alert/lock is produced.
notes: Persistent failed-login counting and threshold lockout are now directly proven, including five bad attempts causing a timed lock. The threshold and lock duration remain hard-coded at 5 attempts/15 minutes rather than governed configurable controls.

requirement: Record authentication, authorisation failure and privileged-action events.
acceptance: Audit search returns complete events with actor and time.
notes: Authentication success/failure, MFA, lockout, permission/step-up/network-denied events are persisted with actor/time/context, and privileged business actions use the audit ledger. Authentication events are not yet integrated into the controlled audit-search/export surface required by the acceptance wording.

requirement: Display the user’s last successful login and active sessions.
acceptance: User/admin can identify unexpected access.
notes: Fresh PostgreSQL evidence proves last successful login is persisted and active sessions expose source IP, user agent, MFA verification and expiry context; /auth/me and /auth/sessions expose the corresponding current-user views.

requirement: Allow authorised administrators to revoke all sessions for a user.
acceptance: Revoked tokens fail immediately or within configured maximum.
notes: Authorised administration can revoke all sessions for a user; fresh PostgreSQL acceptance proves the revoked token fails immediately.

requirement: Prevent shared generic accounts.
acceptance: All production activity maps to a unique human or service identity.
notes: Human account provisioning rejects generic/shared-account naming patterns and automated actions can use attributable non-login/service identities. Complete production evidence that every activity maps to a unique human or scoped service identity remains deployment-dependent.

requirement: Use separate scoped service identities for each internal service.
acceptance: Credential review shows no shared superuser secret.
notes: Database bootstrap defines separate NOLOGIN least-privilege roles for control API and individual worker classes and explicitly avoids committed credentials. Actual production credential review proving distinct rotatable LOGIN identities and no shared superuser secret remains an infrastructure/deployment gate.

requirement: Support IP allowlisting or VPN-only access as a configurable deployment control.
acceptance: Requests outside allowed network are denied when enabled.
notes: IP/CIDR admission is deployment-configurable, trusted-proxy handling is explicit, spoofed forwarding is rejected, and requests outside the configured allowlist receive NETWORK_ACCESS_DENIED while health endpoints remain available.

requirement: Create internal organisation records without creating external portal users.
acceptance: Organisation can be used on campaigns without login credentials.
notes: Internal organisation records are created and used by campaign governance without external portal-user credentials. Fresh PostgreSQL acceptance proves the persistent organisation aggregate is independently usable by the campaign service.

requirement: Store legal/trading name, country, registration reference, industry and status.
acceptance: Required-field validation is enforced.
notes: Legal/trading name, country and status are active model/repository fields and legal-name/email/country-format validation exists. Schema also has registration_reference and industry, but the active organisation model/API/repository does not read or write those fields, so the required record is incomplete.

requirement: Store one or more internal and external contacts with role and communication details.
acceptance: Multiple contacts can be active/effective-dated.
notes: The current organisation aggregate has only one primary contact name/email. No first-class multiple internal/external organisation-contact model with role, communication details and active/effective dating was found.

requirement: Record controller, processor or joint-controller role where known.
acceptance: Campaign consent checks can reference the role.
notes: A controller_role column exists on organisations but is not wired through the active organisation model/repository/API. Consent-review evidence separately records and validates controller role, so campaign consent evidence can carry the role, but it is not yet governed as an organisation-level attribute.

requirement: Record organisation-level restrictions and prohibited purposes.
acceptance: Ineligible campaign purpose is blocked.
notes: Versioned maker-checker organisation policy governs allowed/prohibited campaign purposes. Fresh PostgreSQL acceptance activates the policy and proves a prohibited purpose is rejected by campaign creation while an allowed purpose proceeds.

requirement: Support active, suspended, under-review and closed status.
acceptance: Suspended organisation cannot launch a campaign.
notes: ACTIVE, SUSPENDED, UNDER_REVIEW and CLOSED are explicit lifecycle states. Fresh PostgreSQL acceptance proves status transitions persist with actor evidence and a suspended organisation is rejected by campaign creation; campaign progression and final dispatch also require the organisation to remain ACTIVE.

requirement: Record commercial references such as quote, invoice and payment status.
acceptance: Campaign release policy can require commercial approval.
notes: Campaign commercial records capture quotation/invoice/payment/currency/recipient entitlement and use maker-checker approval. PostgreSQL persistence is exercised and campaign release governance can require the approved campaign-specific commercial entitlement.

requirement: Retain an audit history of organisation changes.
acceptance: Historical values and actor are retrievable.
notes: Versioned organisation events persist actor, reason, event type and before/after status and are retrievable; fresh PostgreSQL acceptance proves that path. Ordinary profile updates do not persist the previous legal/trading/country/contact values, so full historical values cannot be reconstructed from organisation history.

requirement: Prevent accidental duplicate organisation creation.
acceptance: Potential duplicate warning appears based on configured identifiers.
notes: Normalised legal-name plus country duplicate protection exists in memory and PostgreSQL; fresh acceptance proves a normalised duplicate is rejected. The SRS calls for a potential-duplicate warning based on configured identifiers, while current behavior is a fixed hard rejection with no configurable identifier/warning workflow.

requirement: Support organisation-specific data-retention and report branding settings.
acceptance: Generated report uses approved configuration version.
notes: Approved, versioned and effective-dated organisation policy stores contact/campaign retention and report brand/footer settings. No report-generation path was found that consumes those approved branding fields and records the exact policy version used, so the acceptance is not fully met.

requirement: Create a consent review at organisation, source or campaign scope.
acceptance: Reviewer selects the scope and system enforces it.
notes: Consent review explicitly supports ORGANISATION, SOURCE and CAMPAIGN scope with scope-specific validation. PostgreSQL lifecycle acceptance proves a SOURCE-scoped review persists its source identity and governance evidence.

requirement: Record consent collection method, source system, URL/form identifier and date range.
acceptance: Review cannot be approved without required provenance.
notes: Collection method, source system, consent source and collection date range are persisted, and SOURCE scope requires sourceSystem. Submission requires collectionMethod and consentSource. There is no distinct URL/form-identifier field, and sourceSystem is not mandatory for organisation/campaign-scoped reviews, so the exact provenance requirement is not fully enforced.

requirement: Record the consent wording or an immutable reference and wording version.
acceptance: Approved review identifies exact wording/version.
notes: Submission requires both wordingVersion and exactConsentWording; both persist with an approved review. Fresh PostgreSQL acceptance reads them back and revision evidence proves changed wording creates a new governed review.

requirement: Record permitted organisation/controller, purpose, channel and partner use.
acceptance: Campaign outside scope is ineligible.
notes: Organisation, controller role, purpose code, channel, campaign scope and permitted partner organisations are stored. Campaign eligibility enforces organisation, channel, expiry and campaign-specific scope, but does not currently compare campaign purpose against review purposeCode or enforce permittedPartnerOrganisations for organisation/source-scoped reuse.

requirement: Record evidence files or external references with checksums.
acceptance: Evidence tampering can be detected.
notes: Reviews accept governed evidence assets and external evidence references carrying SHA-256 checksums; malformed or non-lowercase checksums are rejected and approved evidence references persist with the review.

requirement: Malware-scan uploaded evidence before availability.
acceptance: Infected/quarantined files cannot be opened or approved.
notes: Uploaded consent evidence resolves only through the trusted-asset path, which requires CLEAN malware-scan state before evidence becomes usable by a review. Existing HTTP/service acceptance exercises trusted evidence resolution.

requirement: Record reviewer, decision, date, expiry and restrictions.
acceptance: Every approval is attributable and time bounded where required.
notes: Independent decision records reviewer, reviewedAt, outcome, expiry, next-review time, restrictions and reason. Approval requires a future expiry; fresh PostgreSQL acceptance proves an attributable time-bounded approved-with-restrictions decision survives persistence.

requirement: Support approved, approved-with-restrictions, rejected, expired and revoked states.
acceptance: State transitions follow policy and are audited.
notes: Approved, approved-with-restrictions, rejected, revoked and superseded transitions are governed and append-only audited. EXPIRED is a valid schema/event state and expiry is enforced dynamically, but no runtime transition was found that moves an approved row to EXPIRED and emits the EXPIRED event.

requirement: Require a reason for rejection, revocation or restriction.
acceptance: Blank reason is blocked.
notes: Decision reason is mandatory for approval/rejection, approved-with-restrictions additionally requires explicit restriction text, and revocation requires a longer reason. Blank/short reasons are rejected by the domain rules; PostgreSQL acceptance proves restriction and revocation reasons persist.

requirement: Support sample-record review notes without storing unnecessary sample PII.
acceptance: Review can be completed using minimised evidence.
notes: Sample review notes are bounded and reject email-address and phone-number patterns; approval can record sampled-record review evidence without retaining unnecessary direct sample PII.

requirement: Require re-review when consent wording, collection method, controller, purpose or source materially changes.
acceptance: Changed version invalidates automatic reuse.
notes: Approved review fields have no mutable edit endpoint. Material changes use the revision workflow: a replacement review is created, the prior review becomes SUPERSEDED and ineligible, and the replacement must be submitted and independently approved. Fresh PostgreSQL acceptance proves lineage, supersession events and reapproval after wording change.

requirement: Link every campaign to a valid consent review or documented non-consent lawful basis where separately approved.
acceptance: Campaign cannot reach release without eligibility reference.
notes: Campaign progression/release requires a valid linked consent review and PostgreSQL release evidence rejects invalid review status/expiry. The SRS also permits a separately approved non-consent lawful-basis alternative; no such governed alternative workflow was found.

requirement: Expose review expiry warnings and block expired approvals.
acceptance: Expiry alert and release block are verified.
notes: Expired review approval is blocked by campaign eligibility/release and fresh PostgreSQL acceptance proves an approved review becomes ineligible after expiresAt. No dedicated advance-expiry warning/alert path was found, so the warning half of the acceptance remains open.

requirement: Allow authorised compliance override only with reason, expiry and second approval.
acceptance: Override is time-bounded and prominently audited.
notes: No authorised compliance override for consent-review eligibility with reason, expiry and independent second approval was found. Existing consent-review revocation requires step-up MFA but is not an eligibility override.

requirement: Maintain one canonical contact for each normalised MSISDN within the configured identity scope.
acceptance: Duplicate import resolves to existing contact.
notes: Duplicate approved imports of the same protected E.164 resolve to one canonical contact. Identity is currently one platform-wide HMAC namespace; a governed configurable identity-scope model is not implemented.

requirement: Normalise MSISDNs to E.164 using country context and validation rules.
acceptance: Known valid/invalid examples pass automated tests.

requirement: Store MSISDN encrypted at application level.
acceptance: Database inspection does not reveal plaintext MSISDN.
notes: PostgreSQL evidence proves the stored identifier is ciphertext, contains no plaintext MSISDN, and decrypts to the canonical E.164 value.

requirement: Store a deterministic keyed HMAC for exact lookup and deduplication.
acceptance: Same canonical MSISDN matches; HMAC cannot be reversed without key.
notes: Keyed HMAC lookup is deterministic and the unique database lookup key resolves duplicate imports to the same canonical contact.

requirement: Display only masked MSISDN to ordinary users.
acceptance: UI and standard exports show configured masking.
notes: Backend/API masking is tested, but the production frontend is deferred, so the UI portion of the acceptance criterion has not been executed.

requirement: Restrict plaintext decryption to the minimum sending/export services and authorised workflows.
acceptance: Permission and service-role tests pass.
notes: Plaintext decryption is constrained to final dispatch and approved privacy/export execution paths. Target-deployment least-privilege service/database identities still require environment evidence.

requirement: Store country, state and LGA using controlled reference data.
acceptance: Invalid state/LGA relationship is rejected or quarantined.
notes: The real import validator rejects an invalid state/LGA relationship as INVALID_GEOGRAPHY; canonical merge resolves geography through controlled reference rows.

requirement: Support unknown/not-provided geography without inventing values.
acceptance: Null/unknown remains distinguishable from invalid.
notes: Missing optional state/LGA remains blank and is distinct from invalid geography. Import staging still requires/defaults a country ISO2, so fully unknown country is not yet represented.

requirement: Store self-declared numeric age and age-recorded timestamp.
acceptance: Record preserves the exact declared value and collection time.
notes: The canonical-contact PostgreSQL test preserves the exact self-declared numeric age and its recorded date.

requirement: Calculate estimated current age using configured approximation rules.
acceptance: Boundary tests for birthdays/partial dates are documented.
notes: No configured estimated-current-age approximation model or birthday/partial-date boundary implementation was found.

requirement: Record age source, verification flag and last-confirmed date.
acceptance: Segment builder can filter by confidence/staleness.
notes: Age source, verification flag and recorded date are stored. The segment builder does not expose confidence/source/verification filters and there is no confidence field or separate governed last-confirmed model.

requirement: Never overwrite the original reported age without retaining history.
acceptance: Attribute history shows old/new values and source.
notes: Two imports update current reported age while retaining both old and new observations with source hashes in profile history.

requirement: Support configurable age-data staleness bands.
acceptance: Segment count changes correctly when threshold changes.
notes: No governed configurable age-staleness bands or segment-count acceptance test for changing a staleness threshold was found.

requirement: Store gender only when provided under an approved data purpose.
acceptance: Unknown/not-provided is supported; no inference occurs.
notes: Gender is optional/self-declared and canonical merge requires an approved review/purpose basis; no inference implementation was found. Explicit per-attribute purpose governance and unknown-gender acceptance evidence remain incomplete.

requirement: Support approved optional attributes such as language and interest category.
acceptance: Attribute catalogue controls type, values and permitted use.
notes: The catalogue supports typed dynamic attributes, allowed values, permissions and safe segmentation queries. A governed end-to-end ingestion/write path for optional dynamic attributes such as interests is not yet evidenced.

requirement: Record attribute source, collected-at time and confidence.
acceptance: Every segmentation attribute has lineage.
notes: Dynamic attribute values record source_system and recorded_at, but no confidence field/model exists and complete segmentation-attribute lineage is not proven end-to-end.

requirement: Support contact active, inactive, invalid, deceased/closed and possible-recycled-number states.
acceptance: Ineligible states are excluded by policy.
notes: The lifecycle supports active, inactive, invalid, recycled, deceased and additional terminal/suppressed states; final dispatch rejects every contact whose status is not ACTIVE.

requirement: Maintain source-system identifiers and import provenance.
acceptance: Contact can be traced back to source batch/record.
notes: The PostgreSQL merge test traces one canonical contact through two source systems/import batches with two durable source links and source-record hashes.

requirement: Merge duplicate contacts through an approved, reversible process.
acceptance: Merge preserves consent and event lineage and creates audit evidence.
notes: Approved import dedup/update is governed and import mutations are captured for controlled rollback, but there is no explicit canonical-contact-to-contact merge workflow proving preservation of two existing contacts consent and event lineage.

requirement: Prevent ordinary users from searching by partial plaintext MSISDN.
acceptance: Only exact authorised lookup or masked search is allowed.
notes: Ordinary contact operations use opaque contact IDs. Permission-guarded privacy workflows require a complete exact E.164 value before HMAC lookup; a partial plaintext MSISDN is rejected.

requirement: Support data correction while preserving history.
acceptance: Correction event identifies source, reason and actor.
notes: PostgreSQL rectification changes the current profile while preserving the old profile with privacy-case ID, executor, reason and original source-system/source-record lineage.

requirement: Support at least 10 million canonical contacts without schema redesign.
acceptance: Scale test meets NFR targets.
notes: High-volume indexes and asynchronous audience materialisation avoid a schema redesign path, but no genuine 10-million-canonical-contact NFR load test has been executed.

requirement: Support CSV and XLSX imports through an internal controlled workflow.
acceptance: Valid template imports successfully.
notes: CSV and bounded XLSX imports run through the same protected validation/staging workflow. XLSX tests cover worksheet selection, hidden sheets, formulas and unsafe embedded/external content.

requirement: Provide downloadable versioned import templates.
acceptance: Template version is recorded on import.
notes: Versioned deterministic CSV and XLSX templates are downloadable through a dedicated controlled API; unknown versions and formats fail closed.

requirement: Support configurable column mapping and saved mappings per source.
acceptance: Repeat source can reuse approved mapping.
notes: Reusable source mappings are governed, maker-checker approved, effective-dated and safely superseded; future replacements do not retire the current mapping before their effective boundary.

requirement: Validate file type, extension, MIME signature, size and malware status.
acceptance: Invalid or disguised file is rejected/quarantined.
notes: Import intake streams to quarantine storage, enforces filename and byte limits, verifies actual CSV/XLSX signatures and records a terminal malware decision before validation can proceed.

requirement: Protect against CSV formula injection in previews and exports.
acceptance: Cells beginning with dangerous formula prefixes are neutralised.
notes: Dangerous spreadsheet prefixes are neutralised in import previews, row-level issue exports, CSV reports and XLSX cell rendering.

requirement: Stream or chunk large files rather than load entire content into memory.
acceptance: Million-row test stays within memory limit.
notes: CSV processing is streaming and production staging is bounded/durable, but the acceptance-required million-row memory-limit run has not been executed.

requirement: Create an immutable import-batch record with checksum, uploader and time.
acceptance: Identical/replayed file is detectable.
notes: PostgreSQL evidence records checksum, uploader and creation time, exact client-request replay returns the original batch, duplicate file checksum is detected, and immutable import identity fields reject direct mutation.

requirement: Validate required fields and controlled values.
acceptance: Row-level reason codes are produced.
notes: Required/type validation produces row-level issue codes; invalid state/LGA relationships are quarantined distinctly while missing optional geography remains missing rather than invented.

requirement: Normalise MSISDN using configured default country only where explicit.
acceptance: Ambiguous numbers are quarantined, not guessed.
notes: MSISDN normalisation supports explicit international numbers and governed country rules; a national number without an explicit recognised country is rejected rather than guessed.

requirement: Detect duplicate rows within the file.
acceptance: Duplicate count and retained row policy are reported.
notes: Durable PostgreSQL staging ranks duplicate lookup HMACs, keeps one canonical staged row, records DUPLICATE_MSISDN issues for later rows and reconciles duplicate counts; preview also detects duplicates before commit.

requirement: Detect contacts already present in the repository.
acceptance: Insert/update/no-change counts reconcile to file total.
notes: Merge distinguishes inserted and updated canonical contacts and preserves source lineage, but there is no first-class unchanged/no-change contact count, so insert/update/no-change cannot yet reconcile exactly as required.

requirement: Support configurable update policy: fill-null, newest-source, trusted-source or manual conflict.
acceptance: Conflicting attributes follow selected policy.
notes: Fill-null, newest-source, trusted-source and manual-conflict policies are implemented; manual conflicts support governed single and atomic batch decisions with optimistic versions.

requirement: Never silently broaden existing consent based on a profile import.
acceptance: Consent changes require consent-specific data and evidence.
notes: A profile import cannot silently broaden consent: PostgreSQL profile updates preserve withdrawn consent, merge requires approved clean consent evidence, and import-derived grants are scoped and recorded with transactional consent events.

requirement: Provide import preview and estimated effects before commit.
acceptance: Operator can cancel before data mutation.
notes: Preview state and cancel-before-canonical-mutation are directly proven in PostgreSQL and HTTP, with staging evidence retained. Preview does not yet estimate repository insert/update/no-change effects before commit.

requirement: Use database bulk-load techniques and bounded transactions.
acceptance: Large import meets throughput target and can recover from failure.
notes: Validation/staging uses bounded batches, PostgreSQL jsonb_to_recordset, leases and restart/retry semantics; merge work is lease-fenced. No large-import throughput target and failure-recovery acceptance run has been executed.

requirement: Provide row-level error export with masked identifiers.
acceptance: Operator can correct only failed rows.
notes: Authorised operators can download bounded row-level validation issues as spreadsheet-safe CSV with masked identifiers and auditable search/export evidence.

requirement: Reconcile uploaded, accepted, rejected, duplicate, inserted, updated and unchanged counts.
acceptance: Counts sum exactly to source rows.
notes: Uploaded, valid, invalid, duplicate, suppressed, inserted and updated totals are persisted/reconciled and conflicts can be closed with immutable evidence. A distinct unchanged-contact count is still outstanding, so exact row-total reconciliation is incomplete.

requirement: Support rollback of an unconsumed erroneous import where legally/operationally safe.
acceptance: Rollback preserves audit and does not delete subsequent independent changes.
notes: Direct PostgreSQL evidence proves rollback rejects an older import after a later independent source, while rolling back the newer import restores prior profile/source lineage, preserves prior active consent, revokes only import-derived consent and records append-only rollback evidence.

requirement: Block campaign use of a batch until required consent review is approved.
acceptance: Unapproved batch cannot create an audience snapshot.
notes: PostgreSQL merge rejects a batch whose consent review is not approved, and the legacy snapshot endpoint no longer trusts caller-supplied members: it derives membership server-side through governed cohort eligibility. An unapproved batch therefore cannot enter canonical audience membership or bypass the snapshot gate.

requirement: Support encrypted import file retention or prompt deletion according to policy.
acceptance: Retention job and audit evidence are verified.
notes: Secure intake derives source expiry from configured retention duration when not supplied internally; lease-fenced deletion removes expired terminal import objects and records append-only success/failure evidence with hashed object keys.

requirement: Represent consent as a separate grant, not a Boolean contact field.
acceptance: One contact can hold multiple scopes independently.
notes: Consent is a separate durable grant ledger; one contact is directly proven to hold multiple independent active consent scopes in PostgreSQL.

requirement: Scope consent to organisation/controller, purpose and channel.
acceptance: Eligibility query requires all configured scope dimensions.
notes: Eligibility requires exact organisation/controller, purpose and channel scope; wrong organisation, purpose or channel is rejected in direct tests and at the final PostgreSQL send check.

requirement: Record grant time, source, wording version and evidence reference.
acceptance: Consent audit view is complete.
notes: PostgreSQL round-trip proves grant/effective time, source type/reference, wording version, evidence object/checksum and creator evidence are retained.

requirement: Support active, pending-verification, expired, withdrawn, revoked and superseded states.
acceptance: Only eligible states are selectable.
notes: All required states exist and ineligible states are rejected by eligibility, but the active ledger service only provides first-class create/withdraw operations for grants; governed EXPIRED, REVOKED and SUPERSEDED transition workflows are not complete.

requirement: Support effective-from and expiry timestamps.
acceptance: Future and expired grants are handled correctly.
notes: Effective-from and expiry timestamps are stored and future/expired grants are directly rejected by eligibility.

requirement: Record consent withdrawal with source, time and scope.
acceptance: Withdrawal affects eligibility immediately.
notes: Withdrawal records actor/source/reason/time through append-only consent events and immediately makes the scoped grant ineligible, including at final dispatch.

requirement: Treat withdrawal as higher priority than an older grant.
acceptance: Event-order tests pass.
notes: Latest effective event semantics make a later withdrawal override an older active grant; direct event-order tests pass.

requirement: Support a new valid grant after withdrawal only with new evidence and timestamp.
acceptance: Old grant is not reactivated.
notes: A later valid re-consent is a new grant with new evidence and later timestamp; the earlier withdrawn grant remains withdrawn and is not reactivated.

requirement: Maintain append-only consent-event history.
acceptance: Current state can be reconstructed from events.
notes: Consent events are append-only in PostgreSQL; create/withdraw event history reconstructs the tested current state and database UPDATE/DELETE attempts are rejected.

requirement: Support global, organisation, purpose and channel suppression scopes.
acceptance: Precedence tests produce expected exclusion.
notes: GLOBAL, ORGANISATION, PURPOSE and CHANNEL suppression scopes each exclude exactly the intended eligibility context; mismatched scope does not exclude.

requirement: Create suppression automatically from recognised STOP replies after confirmation policy.
acceptance: Inbound STOP creates effective suppression and audit event.
notes: Signed inbound replies are resolved through the authoritative recipient relationship; a recognised STOP command creates an immediate idempotent global suppression under the active confirmation policy.

requirement: Support configured STOP synonyms and language variants.
acceptance: Test messages match exact/normalised rules without overmatching ordinary text.
notes: STOP synonyms and language variants are governed through versioned effective-dated maker-checker policy and resolved at inbound execution time.

requirement: Allow manual suppression with reason and authority.
acceptance: Manual action is audited and immediately effective.
notes: Authorised manual suppression with reason is exposed by the consent HTTP workflow, writes SUPPRESSION_CREATED audit evidence and is immediately effective in eligibility.

requirement: Retain minimised suppression identifiers to prevent re-import contact.
acceptance: Deleted profile remains suppressed by HMAC where policy requires.
notes: Real PostgreSQL erasure anonymises the profile while retaining the minimised lookup HMAC, creates one active GLOBAL suppression carrying that HMAC, and uniqueness prevents re-import as a second canonical contact.

requirement: Support invalid-number and possible-recycled-number suppression.
acceptance: Repeated hard failures trigger configured review/suppression.
notes: INVALID and RECYCLED lifecycle statuses can be assigned under authority, but no repeated-hard-failure automation or configured review/suppression trigger was found.

requirement: Run eligibility at segment estimate, snapshot creation and immediately before dispatch.
acceptance: Withdrawal after snapshot but before send is excluded.
notes: Consent/suppression eligibility is compiled for estimate and materialisation/snapshot, while PostgreSQL final eligibility rechecks immediately before dispatch; withdrawal after snapshot is directly proven to hold the queued send.

requirement: Prevent consent review approval from overwriting individual withdrawal.
acceptance: Individual preference always wins.
notes: An approved consent-review basis does not override an individual withdrawal: the final PostgreSQL send check rejects the withdrawn grant while review approval remains present.

requirement: Expose the exact exclusion reason for authorised operations users.
acceptance: Sample excluded contact displays one or more reason codes.
notes: Exact release exclusion reason_code values are durably stored and aggregated, but no authorised operations endpoint was found that displays per-contact exclusion reasons as required by the acceptance example.

requirement: Support configurable consent-expiry and renewal policies.
acceptance: Policy version is recorded with snapshot.
notes: Per-grant expiry is implemented and snapshots record a consentPolicyVersion, but no governed configurable consent-expiry/renewal policy service was found behind that version.

requirement: Provide consent and suppression audit/export for authorised privacy workflows.
acceptance: Export is complete, secured and logged.
notes: Privacy access/export packages include consent and suppression evidence, are encrypted and integrity-checked, log immutable export-request evidence, and the actual HTTP route requires privacy.read plus recent MFA step-up before export work.

requirement: Provide a visual segment builder requiring no SQL access.
acceptance: Authorised operator builds a cohort through UI.
notes: Backend filter/cohort validation, compilation and estimate/materialisation APIs exist, but the required visual no-SQL segment-builder UI is deferred with the frontend programme.

requirement: Support equality, inclusion, exclusion, range, null and recency operators.
acceptance: Each operator has unit and integration tests.
notes: Equality, inclusion/exclusion, range and known/unknown operators are implemented and tested, but there is no true relative-recency operator.

requirement: Support filters for country, state, LGA, age, gender, language, interests, source and consent attributes.
acceptance: Approved fields appear according to attribute catalogue.
notes: Core catalogue covers country/state/LGA, reported age, gender, language and consent purpose, with governed dynamic typed attributes for extensibility. A first-class source filter and distinct consent-status attributes are not implemented.

requirement: Support exact age range such as 18 through 35 using self-declared/estimated age policy.
acceptance: Boundary records at 17,18,35,36 behave correctly.
notes: Fresh PostgreSQL evidence proves reported-age 18..35 is inclusive (17/36 excluded, 18/35 included) and demographic match without consent is excluded. The estimated-age policy/model required by the full requirement is absent.

requirement: Display the age calculation method, source recency and confidence.
acceptance: Operator sees whether age is reported or estimated.
notes: Reported age retains collection date/source and verification metadata, but there is no derived estimated-age method or general confidence model and the operator-facing display remains deferred with the frontend.

requirement: Allow exclusion of age data older than a configurable period.
acceptance: Stale records are counted separately.
notes: AGE_RECORDED_AT is filterable as a date, but there is no governed configurable age-staleness period/policy and no separate stale-record count as required.

requirement: Require active channel/purpose/organisation consent in the eligibility policy.
acceptance: Demographic match alone never becomes final eligibility.
notes: Fresh PostgreSQL cohort evidence proves a demographic match without active matching organisation/purpose/channel consent is excluded; consent is part of the authoritative eligibility query.

requirement: Apply suppression, contact status and frequency caps to final eligibility.
acceptance: Count waterfall reconciles.
notes: Suppression, active contact state and governed frequency caps are enforced in cohort/final eligibility, but the acceptance criterion also requires a reconciled count waterfall, which is not implemented end-to-end.

requirement: Support AND/OR groups with a maximum configurable complexity.
acceptance: Complex rules validate and execute without injection.
notes: Fresh tests prove nested AND/OR, rejection beyond depth/rule bounds and SQL-field injection resistance. The complexity bounds are code constants (depth 5/rules 50), not governed/configurable as required.

requirement: Provide a human-readable summary of the segment logic.
acceptance: Summary accurately represents nested rules.
notes: No implementation was found that renders an accurate human-readable summary of nested segment logic.

requirement: Estimate matching counts without exposing raw MSISDNs.
acceptance: Count result is returned within NFR target.
notes: Cohort estimates return only aggregate eligible count and calculation time without MSISDNs/identities. Required estimate latency/NFR evidence has not been produced.

requirement: Display a count waterfall: demographic, consent, expiry, suppression, cap and final eligible.
acceptance: Totals reconcile with snapshot.
notes: Individual demographic/consent/suppression/cap/final-eligibility controls exist, but there is no single reconciled demographic -> consent -> expiry -> suppression -> cap -> final-eligible count waterfall tied to the snapshot.

requirement: Save, version, clone, retire and compare segment definitions.
acceptance: Historical campaign references remain immutable.
notes: Segment definitions support create/update version history, clone, archive/retire and version comparison; version rows and frozen snapshot references preserve historical definition evidence.

requirement: Restrict segment fields based on user permission and data-use policy.
acceptance: Unauthorised sensitive field is absent or blocked.
notes: Sensitive fields are hidden/rejected through permission-aware registry validation and compilation, including direct backend submission. No distinct governed data-use-policy layer restricting segment fields was found.

requirement: Create an immutable audience snapshot with hash and policy versions.
acceptance: Membership cannot be altered after freeze.
notes: Snapshot hash commits definition/policy/configuration evidence. A fresh RED->GREEN PostgreSQL test proved that before migration 0071 frozen membership accepted UPDATE/DELETE/extra INSERT, while 0071 rejects all three and preserves the frozen member count.

requirement: Store snapshot creation time, rule version and initiating user.
acceptance: Audit view is complete.
notes: Snapshot persistence stores creation time, definition version, consent/configuration policy versions and initiating user. The API does not expose a complete dedicated snapshot audit/read view containing all required evidence.

requirement: Perform final live suppression/consent check before each send.
acceptance: Post-snapshot opt-out is excluded.
notes: Fresh PostgreSQL final-eligibility tests prove queued recipients are rechecked for matching consent/suppression and other safety boundaries immediately before dispatch, so post-snapshot withdrawal/opt-out is excluded.

requirement: Support cohort overlap analysis without exporting identities.
acceptance: System returns counts for intersection and difference.
notes: Snapshot overlap analysis returns intersection, left-only, right-only and union counts without returning contact identities.

requirement: Prevent tiny cohort reporting below configurable privacy threshold.
acceptance: Dashboard groups/suppresses small slices.
notes: A configurable, governed minimum-cohort policy suppresses small demographic/geographic cells in campaign/organisation reports. Equivalent enforcement is not yet applied to cohort estimates/segment previews or a segment dashboard boundary.

requirement: Support asynchronous snapshot creation for multi-million audiences with progress and resumability.
acceptance: Large job can resume without duplicate membership.
notes: Asynchronous materialisation has durable progress, bounded pages, fenced lease/reclaim, restart-safe checkpoints and duplicate-safe final snapshot commit, including PostgreSQL evidence. The acceptance workload has not been demonstrated at multi-million audience scale.

requirement: Create campaigns linked to one internal organisation and consent-review basis.
acceptance: Release is blocked if linkage is missing/invalid.
notes: Campaigns require organisation and consent-review identifiers. Direct PostgreSQL release evidence proves a suspended organisation or rejected consent review blocks recipient release and creates no obligations.

requirement: Store campaign name, purpose, category, owner, requested window and completion deadline.
acceptance: Required data is validated.
notes: Campaign name, purpose, start window, completion deadline and creator identity are governed fields. A separate campaign category and distinct owner field are not present, so the full required metadata set is incomplete.

requirement: Support draft, review, approved, scheduled, dispatching, paused, completed, exception, cancelled and expired states.
acceptance: Invalid transitions are rejected.
notes: The governed state machine implements Draft, approval stages, Scheduled, Dispatching, Paused, Completed, Completed With Exceptions and Cancelled with transition tests. There is no EXPIRED campaign status, so the required lifecycle is not complete.

requirement: Attach exactly one immutable audience snapshot to an approved release version.
acceptance: Approved campaign cannot switch snapshot silently.
notes: Campaign release binds an immutable snapshot and material changes invalidate approvals.

requirement: Compose text, image-caption, video, document and supported provider message types.
acceptance: Capability validation blocks unsupported combination.
notes: Text, image+caption, video and document drafts are accepted with required clean media metadata. Immediately before dispatch each type maps to SEND_TEXT/SEND_IMAGE/SEND_VIDEO/SEND_DOCUMENT and both the frozen provider definition and assigned gateway pool must advertise that capability; missing capability is rejected.

requirement: Store media in object storage with checksum, type, size and scan status.
acceptance: Tampered/quarantined asset cannot be used.
notes: Assets use trusted server-derived checksum, content type, size and malware status; quarantined/revoked/tampered objects fail closed and storage supports filesystem or S3/MinIO.

requirement: Support approved personalisation variables with typed values and fallback.
acceptance: Missing variable follows configured fail/fallback rule.
notes: Variables are declared with governed data types and optional fallbacks. Preview resolves fallbacks and masks sensitive values, while dispatch mode fails closed when a required value is missing or a placeholder is undeclared.

requirement: Preview message using representative test records with masked data.
acceptance: Preview renders all variables.
notes: A preview endpoint renders the exact message template and masks sensitive values by default. Preview values are caller-supplied; no mechanism was found that selects representative approved test records, so the stated representative-record acceptance is not complete.

requirement: Send controlled test messages only to approved test numbers.
acceptance: Production cohort is never used for test send.
notes: Only maker-checker approved test MSISDNs may receive test sends. Test sends freeze the message content hash, explicit OpenWA engine, gateway pool, session, provider adapter and exact provider capability definition/version. Scheduling and worker execution revalidate required capabilities and fail closed on route drift; idempotent replay compares the frozen request.

requirement: Version message text, media, variables and links.
acceptance: Any material edit creates new version.
notes: Message content is append-only by version rather than edited in place. A direct test changes body, variables, links and media across successive drafts, proves versions 1/2/3 with distinct stable hashes, and proves all historical versions remain retrievable.

requirement: Hash the approved message version and include it in campaign release.
acceptance: Dispatch job references exact immutable version.
notes: Approved message content has a deterministic SHA-256 content hash and the campaign aggregate exposes the hash from its frozen approved message version. PostgreSQL release rejects any message version different from the campaign-approved version before creating obligations, so dispatch recipients reference the exact immutable version.

requirement: Require reapproval after material message, media, link, audience, sender or schedule change.
acceptance: Prior approval is invalidated automatically.
notes: Material audience, message, entitlement, transport and schedule changes are explicit, MFA-protected, optimistically versioned, recorded append-only and automatically regress the campaign to the required approval stage.

requirement: Support optional reply/STOP instruction policy by campaign type.
acceptance: Required instruction validation is enforced.
notes: No governed campaign-type reply/STOP instruction policy with required-instruction validation is implemented.

requirement: Support tracked links using a controlled redirect domain and signed identifiers.
acceptance: Link does not expose contact/MSISDN and click is attributable to campaign recipient token.
notes: No controlled tracked-link redirect service with signed recipient-safe attribution is implemented.

requirement: Validate destination URLs against configured safety rules.
acceptance: Disallowed scheme/domain is blocked or requires approval.
notes: Destination links must use HTTPS and, when a governed host allow-list is configured, the destination hostname must be present. Tests prove both unsafe scheme and a valid HTTPS URL on an unapproved domain are blocked while an allow-listed HTTPS domain is accepted.

requirement: Schedule campaigns in a declared timezone and persist UTC.
acceptance: DST and timezone tests produce correct dispatch time.
notes: Campaigns persist UTC start/deadline timestamps plus a declared IANA timezone, and timezone/quiet-hours validation exists. No acceptance-level DST scheduling test or local-time scheduling conversion proof was found, so timezone scheduling closure remains partial.

requirement: Support quiet hours and jurisdiction/organisation sending windows.
acceptance: Jobs outside window remain held.
notes: Per-campaign quiet hours are validated in the campaign timezone and the final pre-send checker detects quiet hours. Organisation/jurisdiction sending-window composition is not implemented, and temporarily blocked queued work is currently suppressed rather than held for the next permitted window.

requirement: Support start, deadline and latest-admission time.
acceptance: Campaign acceptance calculation is recorded.
notes: Requested start and completion deadline are governed and capacity admission computes whether the deadline is achievable. No explicit latest-admission time field or policy exists anywhere in the active repository, so that required scheduling control is missing.

requirement: Allow pause, resume and cancel with reason and authority.
acceptance: State change affects undispatched jobs and is audited.
notes: Pause/resume/cancel are reasoned campaign transitions and final eligibility sees PAUSED state. Undispatched durable-job claims are not campaign-gated and paused queued work is terminally suppressed instead of held, so state changes do not yet have the required complete effect on undispatched jobs.

requirement: Display impact before cancel or audience invalidation.
acceptance: Operator sees sent, in-flight and remaining counts.
notes: The campaign workspace exposes cancellation impact before cancel, including outstanding, already-submitted/cannot-recall and UNKNOWN/reconciliation counts plus warnings. Equivalent impact calculation before audience invalidation is not evidenced.

requirement: Prevent deletion of campaigns with audit or delivery history.
acceptance: Only archive/retire is allowed.
notes: The control API exposes archive/restore for terminal campaigns and no campaign DELETE route was found. There is no direct destructive-delete rejection test tied to campaigns with audit or delivery history, so the acceptance is not promoted from API absence alone.

requirement: Support campaign tags and internal notes with visibility controls.
acceptance: Notes do not leak into client report.
notes: Campaign tags and internal notes are persisted, notes are categorised, and workspace mutations are separated from client-facing campaign fields. There is no explicit note visibility classification or direct client-report leakage regression, so visibility controls are incomplete.

requirement: Support cloning while generating new IDs and requiring fresh approvals.
acceptance: Clone cannot reuse old entitlement or frozen snapshot.
notes: Clone creates a fresh draft ID and strips frozen audience, approved message, commercial approval and final approval evidence. However the clone reuses the source maximum-recipient entitlement by default unless a new value is supplied, so the acceptance requirement that old entitlement cannot be reused is not fully satisfied.

requirement: Support campaign archiving according to retention policy.
acceptance: Archived campaign remains reportable at approved level.
notes: Terminal campaigns can be archived/restored with actor, reason, optimistic versioning and append-only workspace audit events while the underlying campaign/reportable data remains present. Archive timing is not driven by the governed retention-policy subsystem, so retention-policy archival is incomplete.

requirement: Implement configurable approval stages by campaign risk/size/category.
acceptance: Workflow engine selects correct stages.
notes: A fixed approval sequence exists, but there is no configurable approval-stage engine selected by campaign risk, size or category.

requirement: Require consent review approval before audience finalisation.
acceptance: Blocked transition is verified.
notes: Campaign progression cannot start audience build until consent approval, and the service validates the governed consent-review basis before approval.

requirement: Require message/content approval before scheduling.
acceptance: Unapproved version cannot dispatch.
notes: The campaign state machine blocks commercial/final approval and dispatch while the submitted message remains unapproved; scheduling is reached only after message approval.

requirement: Require final campaign release approval by an authorised user.
acceptance: Only permitted role can release.
notes: Final approval requires campaign.approve, recent MFA step-up at the HTTP handler, and an approver different from the campaign creator before the campaign becomes SCHEDULED.

requirement: Enforce maker-checker based on configuration and campaign threshold.
acceptance: Creator cannot self-approve where prohibited.
notes: Four-eyes rules exist for final campaign approval and commercial approval, but they are fixed rules rather than configuration/threshold-driven maker-checker policy.

requirement: Record approval decision, actor, time, comments and object version.
acceptance: Approval evidence is immutable.
notes: Several approval domains record actor/reason/version and some have append-only events, but the complete campaign approval chain does not persist an immutable decision record with actor, time, comments and object version for every approval stage.

requirement: Invalidate approval when approved data changes.
acceptance: Change triggers clear status regression.
notes: Material schedule, transport, audience, message or entitlement amendments regress campaign state and clear downstream approvals according to the changed evidence.

requirement: Record quote, invoice, payment and commercial-approval references without requiring online payment.
acceptance: Finance status is visible and auditable.
notes: Commercial records capture quotation, invoice, payment and approval references through an offline governed workflow; no online payment mechanism is required.

requirement: Optionally block release until payment/commercial approval.
acceptance: Policy switch is effective-dated.
notes: A governed commercial approval can block progression, but the gate is mandatory in the fixed campaign workflow. No effective-dated policy switch was found to make payment/commercial blocking optional.

requirement: Create a campaign entitlement defining maximum unique recipients and messages per recipient.
acceptance: Attempt to exceed entitlement is rejected.
notes: Campaign entitlement fields govern maximum unique recipients and messages per recipient. More than one message per recipient is rejected and PostgreSQL release rejects recipient-count overflow without leaking obligations.

requirement: Tie entitlement to organisation, campaign, snapshot and message version.
acceptance: Entitlement cannot be reused elsewhere.
notes: PostgreSQL release proves the authorised obligation is bound to campaign, organisation, snapshot and message version; reuse with any mismatched binding is rejected.

requirement: Consume/reserve entitlement atomically with recipient ledger creation.
acceptance: Concurrent release cannot over-allocate.
notes: Entitlement checking, recipient-ledger creation and outbox insertion occur in one PostgreSQL transaction. Concurrent releases at a one-recipient ceiling produce one success and one entitlement rejection with exactly one recipient/outbox row.

requirement: Require a new approved entitlement for an additional message or resend outside policy.
acceptance: Second campaign/message is blocked without approval.
notes: The current platform safely prohibits more than one message per recipient and binds release to the approved message version, but it has no workflow for obtaining a new approved entitlement for an additional message or resend outside policy.

requirement: Support emergency stop by authorised role without deleting evidence.
acceptance: Dispatch halts and audit/alerts are generated.
notes: EMERGENCY_STOP is an independently approved maintenance mode that blocks all governed actions and writes append-only maintenance lifecycle evidence. No direct integration was found that generates an operational alert when the emergency stop is activated.

requirement: Support approved exception workflow with reason, expiry and second approval.
acceptance: Exception is visible in report/audit according to policy.
notes: No campaign/policy exception approval object was found that combines reason, expiry, independent second approval and report/audit visibility. Delivery reconciliation exceptions are a different workflow and do not satisfy this requirement.

requirement: Maintain an inventory of genuine sender MSISDNs and WhatsApp account metadata.
acceptance: Every active session maps to one controlled sender record.
notes: A governed PostgreSQL sender inventory exists with controlled account metadata and masked identity, and the embedded gateway maintains session records. Genuine WhatsApp-account/MSISDN evidence has not been established with real paired accounts, so the genuine-account requirement remains externally unproven.

requirement: Store sender MSISDN encrypted and display masked by default.
acceptance: UI/log inspection shows no ordinary plaintext.
notes: A PostgreSQL-backed HTTP test proves plaintext E.164 is AES-GCM encrypted before persistence, only the masked value is returned by create/read models, ciphertext does not equal plaintext, and decrypting the stored ciphertext recovers the original number.

requirement: Record ownership, registration country, profile/display name, recovery information reference and lifecycle status.
acceptance: Operational record is complete without exposing secrets.
notes: New sender sessions require ownership, registration-country, display-name and non-secret recovery-reference metadata. Existing installations remain upgrade-safe through nullable migration columns and can be completed through an MFA-protected optimistic update. Recovery references are write-only and suppressed from ordinary sender JSON and audit evidence; live PostgreSQL tests prove persistence, audit and masking.

requirement: Support logical sender pools that map to one or more actual sender accounts.
acceptance: Operator selects pool; recipient ledger records actual sender.
notes: Logical sender pools map to governed concrete sessions. PostgreSQL allocation evidence proves a recipient obligation is assigned to the actual eligible sender session selected from its logical pool. Multi-pool plans deterministically bind shards to approved pools and retain immutable reallocation evidence.

requirement: Clearly disclose that logical sender is not an alphanumeric WhatsApp sender ID.
acceptance: UI/help text and reports use accurate wording.
notes: The deferred production UI/help/reporting acceptance has not yet proven clear disclosure that a logical sender is not an alphanumeric WhatsApp sender ID.

requirement: Support ready, connecting, disconnected, paused, draining, restricted, retired and quarantined sender states.
acceptance: Scheduler uses only eligible states.
notes: The canonical sender lifecycle is enforced before gateway side effects. Allocation requires eligible READY/BUSY sender state plus a READY non-draining owner node, fresh heartbeats and a live lease; PostgreSQL evidence proves stale/expired ownership is excluded.

requirement: Allow each session to have exactly one active worker lease.
acceptance: Concurrent lease acquisition fails deterministically.
notes: The lease primitive is correct in memory and PostgreSQL: concurrent acquisition yields one owner, expiry permits takeover, and stale fencing versions are rejected. However repository-wide evidence shows PostgreSQLLeaseStore is not wired into a production acquire/renew lifecycle; dispatch consumes lease rows but no runtime caller currently creates or renews them. Operational single-owner leasing is therefore only partial.

requirement: Renew leases through heartbeat and expire stale leases safely.
acceptance: Dead worker becomes unavailable after threshold.
notes: PostgreSQL evidence proves a worker beyond the configured heartbeat TTL and a sender with an expired lease are unavailable for allocation, and the lease store supports fenced renewal/takeover. The missing production wiring is heartbeat-driven lease acquisition/renewal; no runtime caller of PostgreSQLLeaseStore was found, so the requirement remains partial.

requirement: Require manual or controlled recovery before another worker activates an uncertain live session.
acceptance: Split-brain test does not run same session twice.
notes: The gateway send boundary now has direct split-brain evidence: a current lease fence reaches the provider, while an older fence or conflicting authority is rejected before provider submission. Controlled recovery still depends on the currently unwired production lease acquisition/renewal lifecycle, so end-to-end takeover cannot yet be claimed.

requirement: Record worker public/stable IP and infrastructure identity.
acceptance: Operations can trace sessions to nodes.
notes: The node inventory records internal/public network identity, pool, provider, engine, boot and deployed versions. Hostinger/VPS inventory reconciliation remains an external deployment control.

requirement: Allow several sessions per VPS only within configured tested resource limits.
acceptance: Admission control blocks excess placement.
notes: The embedded gateway enforces a configured maximum concurrent-session ceiling and the test suite proves excess session start is rejected. Container resource telemetry is also captured, but admission does not currently use CPU/memory/disk/inode evidence or a tested VPS resource model. Resource-aware multi-session placement therefore remains partial.

requirement: Support per-session proxy settings only for approved stable routing.
acceptance: Configuration is encrypted, audited and tested.
notes: Per-session HTTP/HTTPS/SOCKS proxy configuration is encrypted with the secret keyring, versioned, audited in PostgreSQL, step-up protected for administration, and cannot be changed while the session is READY. Session start resolves the current governed proxy and passes it to the gateway; embedded-gateway tests prove proxy credentials are not persisted in the worker registry or silently reused after control-plane authority changes.

requirement: Maintain per-sender configured and measured safe throughput.
acceptance: Capacity view separates configured cap from observed rate.
notes: Configured safe throughput and runtime pacing are enforced. Observed-rate calibration and live engine-specific capacity evidence still require genuine OpenWA sessions.

requirement: Maintain per-sender hourly/daily safety limits and cooldown.
acceptance: Scheduler stops allocation at limit.
notes: Effective-dated maker-checker pacing policies govern per-session minimum/maximum delay, jitter, hourly and daily submission allowances, cooldown and active-campaign limits. The campaign worker enforces durable counters before provider submission.

requirement: Maintain per-sender failure, disconnect and delivery-health thresholds.
acceptance: Threshold breach pauses or drains sender.
notes: Maker-checker SENDER.HEALTH_THRESHOLDS configuration resolves at sender-session, sender-pool, gateway-pool and platform scope with safe defaults. Health assessment uses measured failure rate, disconnect count, heartbeat recency, successful-delivery recency and capacity evidence. Threshold breach automatically drains an active sender, preventing new allocation while preserving in-flight work; live PostgreSQL integration proves the state transition, optimistic governance version and immutable service-attributed audit event. Genuine WhatsApp telemetry remains required for production calibration of threshold values, not for the implemented enforcement contract.

requirement: Prevent automatic allocation to a newly paired sender until readiness checks pass.
acceptance: Readiness test status is required.
notes: New sessions begin in NEW and must pass pairing, connecting and readiness transitions before allocation.
