requirement: Support sender reservation for a campaign or organisation.
acceptance: Conflicting reservation is rejected.
notes: No first-class campaign- or organisation-level sender reservation workflow with conflict rejection is implemented.

requirement: Support one-active-campaign-per-sender policy as configurable default.
acceptance: Interleaving is blocked unless explicitly enabled/tested.
notes: MaxActiveCampaigns defaults to one when omitted. A PostgreSQL-backed pacing test proves campaign A acquires the sender, campaign B on the same sender is rejected with ErrActiveCampaignLimit, and exactly one ACTIVE sender/campaign assignment remains.

requirement: Provide pairing/QR access only to technical administrators with step-up authentication.
acceptance: Unauthorised role cannot view pairing data.
notes: Pairing QR/code routes require sender.admin and recent MFA step-up. Direct request-level tests prove a sender.read-only user receives 403 without reaching a sensitive pairing handler, and an administrator without recent MFA is stopped by STEP_UP_REQUIRED before lifecycle/QR access.

requirement: Never log session tokens, QR payloads or credentials.
acceptance: Secret scanning/log tests pass.
notes: Gateway logger tests inject a sender MSISDN, QR payload, session token, message content and credential-bearing database URL and prove the sensitive values are removed from output. The repository committed-secret scanner also passes, and embedded-gateway tests prove proxy credentials are not persisted in runtime session registry files.

requirement: Support controlled retirement and secure session-state deletion.
acceptance: Retired sender cannot receive jobs and deletion is evidenced.
notes: Retirement is governed, fenced, blocked while active work exists and evidenced. Cryptographic or storage-level deletion of the real engine session-state volume still requires gateway/runtime implementation and live validation.

requirement: Maintain warm standby workers/senders without counting them as guaranteed capacity until health-checked.
acceptance: Capacity calculation includes only ready capacity.
notes: No explicit warm-standby worker/sender lifecycle exists that excludes standby capacity until a readiness health check promotes it.

requirement: Create one authoritative campaign-recipient record per unique campaign, contact and message version.
acceptance: Database unique constraint blocks duplicates.
notes: PostgreSQL enforces UNIQUE(campaign_id, contact_id, message_version_id). A database-backed release/replay test proves the same release creates exactly one authoritative recipient natural key and one associated outbox row.

requirement: Use a deterministic idempotency key for every recipient obligation.
acceptance: Replayed release/job maps to the same record.

requirement: Create entitlement reservation, recipient record and outbox event atomically.
acceptance: Failure cannot leave untracked queue work or missing queue work.
notes: Recipient authorisation and transactional-outbox creation run in one serializable PostgreSQL transaction. An entitlement-overflow integration test proves an error after attempted recipient creation rolls the whole transaction back to zero recipient and zero outbox rows.

requirement: Publish execution jobs from a transactional outbox.
acceptance: Outbox publisher can resume after crash.
notes: A PostgreSQL crash-recovery test leaves an outbox row leased by publisher A, reclaims it with publisher B after lease expiry, advances the fence, safely replays publication, creates exactly one durable job, and completes the outbox as PUBLISHED.

requirement: Use Redis/BullMQ or equivalent only as execution queue, not source of truth.
acceptance: Queue can be rebuilt from PostgreSQL state.
notes: Campaign recipients and transactional outbox remain authoritative in PostgreSQL and queue publication is replay-safe while the outbox is pending/processing. There is no mechanism to reconstruct a durable job that is lost after its outbox record is already PUBLISHED, so complete queue rebuild from authoritative eligible state is not proven.

requirement: Partition large campaigns into bounded dispatch shards.
acceptance: Five-million-recipient campaign does not create one unmanageable transaction/job.
notes: An explicit five-million-recipient test completes as 1,000 bounded release calls of at most 5,000 recipients each. Deterministic sharding with a 10,000-recipient target remains within 500 shards rather than creating one unbounded transaction or job.

requirement: Claim jobs atomically with lease/visibility timeout.
acceptance: Two workers cannot process the same job concurrently.
notes: Real PostgreSQL FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED claiming gives exactly one concurrent owner. After lease expiry a second worker reclaims the job with an advanced fence, and the stale owner cannot complete it.

requirement: Allocate jobs only to ready sender sessions with available capacity.
acceptance: Ineligible sender receives no job.
notes: PostgreSQL allocation assigns only a fresh READY/capable sender. The integration test proves stale worker heartbeat, exhausted daily sender capacity, and expired sender lease each result in ErrNoHealthySession.

requirement: Respect campaign schedule, quiet hours, deadline and pause state at dispatch time.
acceptance: Held jobs remain unsent.
notes: The final pre-send PostgreSQL check correctly detects PAUSED, future-start, deadline-passed and quiet-hours states before gateway submission. However the dispatch handler currently converts every ineligible decision into SUPPRESSED_BEFORE_SEND, so temporary schedule/pause holds become terminal suppression instead of remaining held for later dispatch.

requirement: Perform a final consent, suppression and contact-status check before submission.
acceptance: Late withdrawal is excluded.
notes: Immediately before submission the authoritative PostgreSQL checker re-reads contact status, suppressions and current consent. Integration evidence proves inactive contact, global suppression and consent withdrawal are excluded, while the handler test proves an excluded recipient never reaches the gateway.

requirement: Apply per-sender rate and in-flight limits.
acceptance: Load test demonstrates bounded throughput.
notes: Per-sender governed pacing, hourly/daily allowances, active-campaign limits, message-type overrides and in-flight constraints exist. No acceptance-level load test demonstrates bounded throughput under sustained load, so the stated acceptance is not yet proven.

requirement: Record every delivery attempt separately from final recipient state.
acceptance: Retry history is preserved.
notes: A PostgreSQL retry-history test executes two submission attempts and proves all six ordered delivery events remain in delivery_events while the authoritative recipient ends at GATEWAY_ACCEPTED with AttemptCount=2.

requirement: Use configurable retry policy by failure category.
acceptance: Permanent errors are not retried; transient errors follow backoff.
notes: Gateway failures are explicitly classified SAFE_TO_RETRY, PERMANENT or OUTCOME_UNKNOWN; permanent errors do not retry and safe transient failures enter the durable retry path. The active platform has no governed configurable retry policy by failure category, so the configurability requirement remains incomplete.

requirement: Apply exponential/backoff with jitter for infrastructure errors.
acceptance: Retry schedule follows configured bounds.
notes: Durable retryable jobs use bounded exponential fallback backoff and persisted available_at scheduling. Retry jitter and governed/configured retry-backoff bounds are not implemented in the active job retry path; sender pacing jitter is a different concern.

requirement: Avoid automatic resend after an uncertain provider outcome.
acceptance: Unknown outcome enters reconciliation/manual policy.
notes: Uncertain outcomes remain reconciliation-required and can only be resolved through an MFA-protected, evidence-backed operator action; confirmed non-submission is blocked when provider evidence exists.

requirement: Support safe operator retry only when duplicate risk is understood and approved.
acceptance: Retry action displays risk and records approval.
notes: Evidence-backed manual reconciliation exists and CONFIRM_NOT_SUBMITTED refuses retry when provider correlation/acknowledgement indicates duplicate risk; operator action is audited. The acceptance specifically requires retry risk to be displayed and approval recorded, and no complete risk-display/approval workflow is evidenced.

requirement: Support campaign pause that stops new claims while allowing controlled treatment of in-flight jobs.
acceptance: Pause semantics are tested.
notes: Campaign pause/resume is modelled, audited by execution events, and PAUSED is detected at the final pre-send check. New durable-job claims are not campaign-gated, and already queued paused work is currently terminally suppressed rather than held for controlled in-flight treatment, so pause semantics are incomplete.

requirement: Support campaign cancellation that marks undispatched obligations cancelled and preserves attempts.
acceptance: Counts reconcile after cancellation.
notes: No campaign-cancellation workflow currently marks all undispatched obligations CANCELLED while preserving attempts and reconciling counts.

requirement: Recover expired claims without losing or duplicating obligations.
acceptance: Worker-kill test passes.
notes: PostgreSQL evidence proves an abandoned processing claim is recoverable after lease expiry, lease fencing advances, and the stale owner cannot complete the recovered job. The acceptance asks for an actual worker-kill/restart test, which has not been demonstrated.

requirement: Reconstruct missing queue jobs from authoritative eligible states.
acceptance: Queue-loss recovery test returns expected count.
notes: No authoritative reconstruction workflow recreates missing queue jobs after queue loss for obligations whose outbox publication has already completed.

requirement: Expose queue depth and oldest-job age by campaign/shard/sender.
acceptance: Operations dashboard and alerts work.
notes: Operations exposes global queue depth and oldest queued timestamp and supports governed queue-depth alerting. The required queue depth/oldest-job dimensions by campaign, shard and sender are not exposed, so the dashboard/alert acceptance is only partial.

requirement: Prioritise jobs using configurable campaign priority without starving normal campaigns.
acceptance: Scheduler fairness test passes.
notes: Durable jobs carry a numeric priority and claims order higher priority first. There is no governed configurable campaign-priority policy and no fairness/starvation acceptance test proving normal campaigns continue to progress.

requirement: Reserve capacity for high-priority campaigns only through explicit policy.
acceptance: Reservation is visible and audited.
notes: Explicit approved routing plans create visible HELD/ACTIVE/RELEASED per-pool capacity reservations with rate/hourly/daily units and fencing. No high-priority-only policy binding or reservation-specific append-only audit trail was found; routing-plan approval metadata alone does not fully prove the reservation audit acceptance.

requirement: Forecast completion using remaining jobs and measured available capacity.
acceptance: Forecast updates as throughput changes.
notes: Forecast recomputes remaining work and measured available capacity on every assessment. A direct coordinator test proves reducing measured throughput from 20 to 10 messages/minute moves projected completion later and updates the effective-throughput evidence.

requirement: Reject or flag campaigns whose required rate exceeds measured safe capacity.
acceptance: Admission decision and assumptions are recorded.
notes: Admission compares required rate/volume against measured rate and daily capacity with a safety margin and returns ADMIT/HOLD/REJECT with reasons. PostgreSQL evidence proves the capacity reference, evidence version, remaining volume, measured capacity, safety margin, required/effective rate, forecast, deadline, decision, reasons and evaluation time are durably recorded.

requirement: Authenticate provider/gateway events using signature or trusted channel.
acceptance: Invalid signature is rejected and alerted.
notes: Gateway delivery and inbound callbacks are authenticated over exact body bytes with HMAC, bounded timestamp validation and dual-key rotation support; invalid signatures are rejected. No dedicated security alert/audit path for an invalid gateway signature was found, so the acceptance requirement that rejection is also alerted is not fully closed.

requirement: Require event identifier, provider message identifier, type and occurrence time where available.
acceptance: Malformed event is quarantined.
notes: The versioned callback contract requires eventId, supported eventType and occurredAt, and requires providerMessageId for acknowledgement states while allowing a safe clientReference fallback. Unknown fields, missing identifiers and weak evidence are rejected with 400/422 responses, but malformed provider events are not durably quarantined for later review.

requirement: Deduplicate repeated provider events.
acceptance: Duplicate webhook does not increment metrics twice.
notes: PostgreSQL enforces one durable event per deduplication key and binds the key to an immutable fingerprint. Fresh PostgreSQL acceptance proves replay of the same provider event does not create another event or increment campaign metrics twice, while conflicting reuse is rejected.

requirement: Handle out-of-order events using monotonic state precedence and event history.
acceptance: Delivered-before-sent event results in valid final state.
notes: The delivery reducer uses monotonic acknowledgement precedence and preserves each accepted event in delivery_events. State-machine acceptance proves delivered-before-sent remains DELIVERED, and PostgreSQL acceptance proves the durable event history is retained.

requirement: Preserve raw redacted event metadata for diagnosis according to retention.
acceptance: Authorised user can inspect without secrets/PII leakage.
notes: Delivery events retain minimised provider event/message identifiers, canonical type/time and bounded error metadata, with time-key indexing/partition-readiness for retention operations. The system does not preserve a separately redacted raw provider envelope and exposes no dedicated authorised diagnostic event-inspection surface governed by an event-retention policy.

requirement: Map provider-specific states and errors to canonical statuses/reason codes.
acceptance: Contract tests cover mapping.
notes: Known OpenWA sent/ack/delivered/read/failed states are normalised into the canonical gateway event contract and bounded canonical error codes. Direct contract coverage for the provider-specific mapping table/reason taxonomy is incomplete, and current OpenWA failure mapping is coarse rather than a fully governed retryable/permanent reason catalogue.

requirement: Correlate events using provider ID and fallback identifiers where safe.
acceptance: Unmatched events enter reconciliation queue.
notes: Gateway events correlate by control-plane clientReference first and safely fall back to providerMessageId; contradictory evidence on known recipients is surfaced for governed reconciliation. An event that cannot resolve by either identifier currently returns CAMPAIGN_RECIPIENT_NOT_FOUND rather than entering a durable unmatched-event reconciliation queue, so the exact acceptance is incomplete.

requirement: Never downgrade a terminal higher-confidence state because of a late lower state.
acceptance: State machine tests pass.
notes: State-machine tests prove lower-confidence late progress/ack/failure events cannot downgrade stronger SENT/DELIVERED/READ evidence. Contradictory late evidence is retained as reconciliation-required instead of rewriting the higher-confidence state.

requirement: Process inbound STOP and configured opt-out commands promptly.
acceptance: Suppression is active within target time.
notes: Authenticated inbound messages are checked synchronously against the governed opt-out keyword policy. The signed inbound STOP acceptance test proves suppression is created idempotently before the callback returns, while a non-command does not suppress.

requirement: Store inbound replies with minimised content and access restrictions.
acceptance: Only authorised operations users can view.
notes: Inbound replies are encrypted at rest, content reveal uses a separate inbound.content.read permission and audited reveal path, retention redacts plaintext while preserving minimised fingerprint/operational evidence, and legal hold prevents premature content deletion.

requirement: Support manual classification/escalation of replies where required.
acceptance: Action is audited.
notes: Authorised inbound.review users can classify QUESTION/COMPLAINT/OPT_OUT/OTHER, mark escalation, require an escalation reason, and persist reviewer/time/version evidence. The review/classification mutation does not append a dedicated immutable audit event, so the acceptance that the action is audited is not fully met.

requirement: Run scheduled reconciliation for submitted/pending/unknown records.
acceptance: Stale records are resolved or surfaced.
notes: UNKNOWN and reconciliation-required recipients are surfaced in the operations exception/backlog views and support governed manual resolution. The scheduled delivery reconciliation worker currently reconciles campaign metric counts rather than polling/resolving stale SUBMITTING/GATEWAY_ACCEPTED/UNKNOWN provider outcomes, so scheduled status reconciliation is incomplete.

requirement: Declare final unknown only after configured reconciliation window.
acceptance: Premature finalisation is prevented.
notes: Safety behavior records an ambiguous provider outcome as UNKNOWN immediately and prevents blind resend, but there is no separate provisional-versus-final UNKNOWN lifecycle or governed reconciliation window that must elapse before finalisation.

requirement: Record discrepancy between gateway acceptance and later delivery outcome.
acceptance: Campaign metrics expose the funnel.
notes: Recipients preserve highestAcknowledgement, contradiction count and reconciliation-required evidence when later outcomes conflict with earlier gateway/provider acknowledgement. Campaign metrics expose Submitted/Sent/Delivered/Read/Failed/Unknown funnel stages, but GATEWAY_ACCEPTED is folded into Submitted and there is no distinct acceptance-versus-later-outcome discrepancy metric.

requirement: Support bulk provider-status import/reconciliation if an adapter later provides it.
acceptance: Interface supports asynchronous status source.
notes: No first-party asynchronous bulk provider-status import/reconciliation adapter contract was found. Current status ingestion is callback/event based plus governed manual exception resolution.

requirement: Provide campaign dashboard with audience, dispatch, delivery, engagement and performance sections.
acceptance: Dashboard loads for a large campaign within NFR target.
notes: Backend dashboard/report data exists for audience, delivery, engagement, exceptions and operations, but no frontend large-campaign dashboard NFR timing evidence proves the acceptance target.

requirement: Show uploaded/imported, valid, duplicate, invalid, suppressed, consent-ineligible, capped and final-eligible counts.
acceptance: Waterfall reconciles to source/snapshot totals.
notes: Import reconciliation covers uploaded, valid, invalid, duplicate and suppressed rows with balanced totals, but the required consent-ineligible, capped and final-eligible waterfall is not represented end-to-end.

requirement: Show authorised, queued, claimed, submitted, gateway-accepted, sent, delivered, read, failed, unknown and cancelled counts.
acceptance: State totals reconcile to recipient ledger.
notes: The recipient ledger has the required delivery states, but campaign aggregate/report output collapses CLAIMED into queued and GATEWAY_ACCEPTED into submitted and does not expose cancelled as a distinct aggregate.

requirement: Do not label submitted or gateway-accepted messages as delivered.
acceptance: UI/report terminology tests pass.
notes: Report terminology directly keeps submitted and delivered distinct, but frontend/UI terminology evidence is deferred and therefore the combined UI/report acceptance is not fully closed.

requirement: Show denominator and definition for every rate.
acceptance: Hover/export includes formula.
notes: No report/dashboard model was found that exposes a denominator and formula definition for every rate in hover/export form.

requirement: Show current, average and peak submission throughput.
acceptance: Metrics match event/time-bucket data.
notes: No campaign report/dashboard implementation was found for current, average and peak submission throughput reconciled to event/time-bucket data.

requirement: Show queue depth, oldest job age and forecast completion.
acceptance: Forecast updates at configured interval.
notes: Queue depth and oldest queued job evidence exist and execution forecasts react to measured throughput changes, but they are not proven as one campaign dashboard view refreshing at a governed/configured interval.

requirement: Show actual start, completion and deadline variance.
acceptance: Completed campaign report includes timestamps.
notes: Campaign report exposes actual execution start and completion timestamps, but it does not expose completion-deadline variance as a report field.

requirement: Show retry count, retry rate and major failure reasons.
acceptance: Reason totals reconcile to attempts.
notes: Retry attempts and failure details are durable, but campaign report/dashboard does not yet aggregate retry count, retry rate and major failure reasons with attempt reconciliation.

requirement: Show sender allocation, success, failure, delivery ratio, latency and reconnect count.
acceptance: Sender roll-up equals campaign totals where applicable.
notes: Campaign pool report exposes sender-pool allocation and delivery/failure/unknown counts, but success ratio, latency and reconnect count roll-ups required by the acceptance are missing.

requirement: Show geography and demographic breakdowns using snapshot attributes.
acceptance: Lagos/age segment report matches membership.
notes: State/LGA/gender/age breakdowns reconcile to campaign recipient membership in PostgreSQL, including UNKNOWN buckets, but the SQL reads current contact attributes rather than frozen snapshot attributes; historical/as-of demographic reporting is therefore not closed.

requirement: Apply configurable minimum-cohort privacy threshold.
acceptance: Small cells are suppressed/combined.
notes: Minimum cohort thresholds are governed and versioned. PostgreSQL report evidence proves a threshold of two leaves Lagos=2 visible while all one-person demographic/geographic cells are suppressed and raw breakdowns do not escape the reporting boundary.

requirement: Show replies, opt-outs and link clicks where reliably available.
acceptance: Metric definition states collection limitations.
notes: Opt-out counts are reported and inbound/reply handling exists elsewhere, but link-click collection is not implemented and report metric definitions do not explicitly document collection limitations.

requirement: Maintain incremental aggregate counters rather than rescan all recipient rows for each dashboard load.
acceptance: Performance test verifies bounded query plan.
notes: Delivery transitions update campaign_metrics incrementally inside the same PostgreSQL transaction, avoiding recipient rescans for core counters. The acceptance additionally requires a bounded-query-plan performance test, which is not yet present.

requirement: Make metric event consumers idempotent.
acceptance: Replay does not double-count.
notes: A PostgreSQL replay test proves an identical delivery event is stored once and does not apply a second metric delta; queued/submitted counters remain unchanged on replay.

requirement: Provide near-real-time updates with configurable refresh interval.
acceptance: Update latency meets NFR.
notes: No evidence currently proves configurable near-real-time campaign dashboard refresh or that update latency meets the stated NFR.

requirement: Generate an organisation-facing campaign report without portal access.
acceptance: Authorised user can export approved report.
notes: An authorised user can request an organisation-facing campaign report, a separate checker approves/freeze-snapshots it, and the export worker renders it for short-lived retrieval without portal access.

requirement: Support PDF-ready, XLSX and CSV report data outputs.
acceptance: Generated files open and totals match.
notes: CSV, PDF and XLSX renderers produce structurally valid files. A direct regression proves the same delivered total survives all three report formats.

requirement: Exclude internal notes, secrets, raw error payloads and unnecessary MSISDNs from client report.
acceptance: Report-content security test passes.
notes: A PostgreSQL-backed report-content security test injects campaign internal notes, organisation internal notes, raw provider error detail and an unnecessary MSISDN-like value and proves none appear in JSON or CSV client report output.

requirement: Support approved branding and explanatory caveats.
acceptance: Report template version is recorded.
notes: Export requests record template version and support watermark/caveat-like warning content, but no governed approved-branding model/approval evidence was found.

requirement: Allow campaign report regeneration from retained summary data.
acceptance: Archived campaign can reproduce approved metrics.
notes: Campaign/report data is retained and terminal campaigns can be archived without deleting authoritative rows, but archived-report regeneration from retained summary data is not directly proven and current demographic breakdowns depend on mutable contact attributes.

requirement: Record report generator, time, version and checksum.
acceptance: Report audit record is complete.
notes: Export records contain request/approval actors, template version, generated time and output SHA-256, but the completing worker/generator identity is not retained as a complete report audit field and no acceptance-level complete-audit-record test exists.

requirement: Support masked recipient-level exception export for authorised operations.
acceptance: Export is permissioned, encrypted and logged.
notes: No campaign recipient-level exception export matching the permissioned, encrypted, logged and masked acceptance was found in the active implementation.

requirement: Expose metric-quality flags for incomplete provider events or reconciliation gaps.
acceptance: Report cannot imply false completeness.
notes: Reports warn when campaign metrics are unavailable and when UNKNOWN outcomes require reconciliation, preventing some false-completeness claims. Metric reconciliation drift is detected/recorded but is not surfaced in the campaign report, so reconciliation-gap quality flags are incomplete.

requirement: Provide an internal configuration catalogue with typed values and validation.
acceptance: Invalid configuration cannot be activated.
notes: The internal configuration catalogue enforces key/scope rules, canonical JSON, checksums, lifecycle and consumer-specific safety validation, but it has no first-class per-key typed schema/value-type registry; generic valid JSON is therefore broader than the SRS typed-catalogue requirement.

requirement: Version and effective-date material configuration.
acceptance: Campaign records policy/config version used.
notes: PostgreSQL configuration versions are effective-dated and resolve deterministically; audience/routing/provider evidence freezes material versions. However campaigns.configuration_versions exists in schema but the active campaign model/repository does not read or write that generic field, so the exact campaign-record acceptance is not fully met.

requirement: Require approval for security, consent, retention, throughput and retry policy changes.
acceptance: Maker-checker is enforced.
notes: Maker-checker is enforced for common security/runtime, consent/STOP, retention, throughput and reporting-privacy policies. Retry/reconciliation/UNKNOWN-window settings are still partly fixed/deployment configuration, so approval governance is not complete across every named policy class.

requirement: Support rollback to a prior configuration version.
acceptance: Rollback is audited and deterministic.
notes: Fresh PostgreSQL acceptance proves approved effective-dated replacement plus rollback creates a new governed version, requires independent approval, preserves rollback/supersession evidence and resolves the prior value deterministically at the rollback effective time.

requirement: Configure consent purposes, channels, expiry and review rules.
acceptance: New purpose can be added without code change.
notes: Consent purposes/channels are data-driven rows and campaigns/imports enforce their linked consent review, so adding purpose data does not require a code constant. There is no complete governed purpose-administration service/API covering purpose, channel, expiry and review-rule configuration end to end.

requirement: Configure age staleness and estimation policy.
acceptance: Segment engine uses active version.
notes: No governed age-estimation/staleness policy exists and the segment engine does not resolve an active age-policy version. Current logic uses self-declared reported age/recorded date only.

requirement: Configure state/LGA reference data and validation.
acceptance: Reference update preserves historical codes.
notes: State/LGA validation and stable reference codes exist, including rejection of invalid relationships, but the active geography catalogue is effectively seeded/read-only and no governed reference-data update workflow proves historical-code preservation after administrator changes.

requirement: Configure suppression precedence and STOP keywords.
acceptance: Policy test suite can be rerun.
notes: Versioned effective-dated maker-checker STOP keyword policy is configurable and re-testable; suppression/withdrawal precedence is enforced again at the final PostgreSQL eligibility boundary.

requirement: Configure frequency caps by organisation/purpose/channel.
acceptance: Eligibility reflects cap.
notes: Governed organisation/purpose/channel frequency-cap policy is effective-dated and eligibility/final dispatch enforce the active cap.

requirement: Configure campaign approval thresholds and roles.
acceptance: Workflow changes without deployment.
notes: Campaign approval has RBAC, fixed staged transitions and four-eyes final approval, but there is no governed configurable threshold/risk/category-to-role engine; changing the approval workflow still requires code/deployment.

requirement: Configure sender/session limits, rate caps and health thresholds.
acceptance: Worker scheduler receives versioned settings.
notes: Sender/session rate, concurrency, allowance, cooldown/recovery and health thresholds are governed/versioned. Fresh PostgreSQL evidence proves the worker pacing controller resolves the approved policy and persists the exact policy ID/version into sender_pacing_runtime.

requirement: Configure retry, reconciliation and unknown-outcome windows.
acceptance: Dispatch follows active policy.
notes: Retry, UNKNOWN handling and reconciliation mechanisms exist, but important backoff/reconciliation windows remain fixed or deployment-environment settings rather than one approved effective-dated runtime policy consumed by dispatch.

requirement: Configure report templates, privacy thresholds and retention.
acceptance: Generated report reflects version.
notes: Reporting privacy thresholds and retention are governed/versioned and report outputs carry privacy policy evidence, but administrator-defined/versioned report-template composition is not implemented end to end.

requirement: Record business and security audit events append-only.
acceptance: Ordinary users cannot update/delete audit events.
notes: Fresh PostgreSQL acceptance proves business/security audit events are appended and ordinary UPDATE/DELETE attempts are rejected by database triggers.

requirement: Include actor, action, object, before/after summary, reason, IP/device, time and correlation ID in audit where applicable.
acceptance: Audit completeness tests pass.
notes: The audit model and PostgreSQL round-trip preserve actor, action, object, before/after, reason, IP/device, time and correlation ID when supplied, with a direct completeness test. Comprehensive proof that every applicable administrative/business path supplies all applicable context is still absent.

requirement: Provide searchable audit views with export controls.
acceptance: Auditor can trace one campaign end to end.
notes: Audit search supports actor/action/object/org/outcome/sensitivity/correlation/IP/time filters and controlled export, but there is no single composed acceptance test demonstrating an auditor can reconstruct one campaign end to end across consent, approval, dispatch and reporting.

requirement: Protect audit integrity using restricted roles and tamper-evident chaining or external archival.
acceptance: Integrity validation detects alteration.
notes: Audit storage is append-only, service-role access is explicit, and the persisted hash chain now canonicalises JSON/IP/timestamp representation. Fresh PostgreSQL verification passes and direct UPDATE/DELETE tampering is rejected.

requirement: Alert on privileged configuration changes and audit-control failures.
acceptance: Test alert is delivered.
notes: Governed operational alert policies, escalation and delivered portal notifications exist, but there is no dedicated signal/test proving privileged configuration changes or audit-integrity/control failures trigger an alert.

requirement: Support authorised exact contact lookup using HMAC and controlled decryption.
acceptance: DSAR operator can locate a known number.
notes: Privacy cases normalise a complete E.164 subject, derive the protected lookup HMAC and resolve the canonical contact without partial plaintext search. Fresh PostgreSQL acceptance proves a known number maps to the expected contact ID while the externally visible subject remains masked; plaintext decryption is confined to approved package execution.

requirement: Provide a data-subject access package containing profile, sources, consent, suppression and campaign history according to policy.
acceptance: Package is complete and secure.
notes: Approved access cases encrypt a subject package containing the current profile/source fields, attribute source data, consent, suppressions and campaign history. However the package model/query does not expose the separate contact_sources provenance/history records maintained by imports, so the exact SRS requirement for profile, sources, consent, suppression and campaign history is not fully closed.

requirement: Support correction requests with source/reason and history.
acceptance: Current value changes without erasing audit.
notes: Approved rectification allows only governed fields and preserves the complete pre-change profile with privacy case, actor, reason and original source provenance. Fresh PostgreSQL acceptance proves the current value changes while attributed history remains intact.

requirement: Support objection/opt-out with immediate effective suppression.
acceptance: Future eligibility is blocked.
notes: Approved objection execution atomically marks the contact SUPPRESSED and creates one effective GLOBAL WHATSAPP suppression on the subject lookup HMAC. Fresh PostgreSQL acceptance proves that mutation, while final-dispatch PostgreSQL acceptance independently proves active suppression/contact ineligibility blocks future sends.

requirement: Support deletion/anonymisation workflow subject to lawful retention and suppression requirements.
acceptance: Decision records retained; unnecessary PII removed.
notes: Erasure is blocked by active legal hold, removes unnecessary attributes/profile PII, withdraws active consent, replaces the encrypted MSISDN payload, marks the contact ANONYMISED/restricted, preserves the lookup HMAC and creates a minimised global suppression. PostgreSQL acceptance proves the original PII is removed while suppression identity and the completed decision record remain.

requirement: Support contact export in structured format for approved portability requests.
acceptance: Export is controlled and logged.
notes: Approved portability/access execution creates an encrypted structured package with integrity hash. Fresh PostgreSQL acceptance proves ExportEnvelope appends the authoritative EXPORT_REQUESTED event; the delivery path is actor-bound, expiring, single-use and audited, and the HTTP route enforces privacy permission plus recent MFA step-up.

requirement: Track DSAR status, deadlines, owner and evidence.
acceptance: Overdue alert is produced.
notes: Privacy cases persist status, requested/due times, assignee/owner and immutable lifecycle evidence, with indexes for open-case due-date queries. No backend worker/alert policy currently produces an overdue DSAR alert, so the exact acceptance remains incomplete.

requirement: Restrict disclosure of third-party or security-sensitive information.
acceptance: Review step exists before release.
notes: Disclosure-producing access/portability cases require submission, independent approval and a separate executor; maker cannot approve and checker cannot execute their own decision. Ordinary case JSON excludes encrypted result material, and controlled export additionally requires permission and recent MFA step-up, providing the required review gate before release.

requirement: Support retention holds and legal holds with approval.
acceptance: Scheduled deletion excludes held records and logs reason.
notes: Legal holds use draft, submission, independent approval/rejection, active and release states with immutable reasoned events. Fresh PostgreSQL retention acceptance proves scheduled privacy-case deletion excludes an otherwise-due case under an active hold. The scheduler currently filters held records silently and does not append a dedicated skip/hold reason for that deletion decision, so the exact logging portion remains incomplete.

requirement: Provide privacy-impact and data-inventory reports.
acceptance: System can identify categories, purposes, sources and retention.
notes: No first-class privacy-impact/data-inventory report currently identifies the required data categories, processing purposes, source provenance and retention policy in one governed report.

requirement: A demographic match alone never authorises a campaign send.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: A PostgreSQL release test gives a contact demographic age/gender values but removes consent; release produces zero obligations and a NO_ACTIVE_CONSENT exclusion. Demographic match alone cannot authorise communication.

requirement: Eligibility requires a valid organisation/controller, purpose and channel basis plus no overriding suppression.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: Final eligibility directly rejects mismatched organisation, purpose or channel basis and independently rejects active suppression. Only the matching WhatsApp organisation/purpose basis with no overriding suppression remains eligible.

requirement: An individual withdrawal overrides an earlier or organisation-level approval.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: A queued recipient with previously active consent becomes ineligible immediately after the grant is WITHDRAWN; the final pre-send check returns CONSENT_WITHDRAWN before provider submission.

requirement: The same campaign/message version shall not be sent more than once to the same contact unless a separately approved resend is created.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: Natural-key/release replay and durable gateway idempotency prevent duplicate same-version submission, including concurrent calls and gateway restart. No separately approved resend workflow was found, so the explicit exception path in the rule is not implemented.

requirement: An audience snapshot is immutable; changes require a new snapshot and approval.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: PostgreSQL rejects audience-snapshot UPDATE and DELETE. The additional rule that every changed audience must be materialised as a new snapshot and pass a new approval cycle is not yet directly proven end-to-end.

requirement: A message version is immutable after approval; any material change creates a new version.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: PostgreSQL rejects mutation of an approved message version; message-service evidence proves material body/variable/link/media changes create successive immutable versions with distinct hashes.

requirement: Campaign entitlement cannot be transferred or reused by another campaign.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: An approved entitlement for campaign A is rejected when campaign B attempts to validate/reuse it, while campaign A continues to validate the same approval.

requirement: Gateway acceptance does not equal sent, delivered or read.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: The delivery state machine treats gateway acceptance, sent, delivered and read as distinct monotonic evidence states and does not infer later acknowledgements from earlier ones.

requirement: Only actual registered WhatsApp MSISDNs may be used as OpenWA senders.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: The platform has governed sender inventory and real OpenWA session plumbing, but acceptance requires proof against genuinely authenticated WhatsApp-registered MSISDN accounts. That is a live external gate, not something embedded tests can prove.

requirement: A logical sender pool is an internal routing abstraction, not a recipient-facing alphanumeric sender ID.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: Campaigns use logical sender-pool abstractions for routing while the actual governed sender session remains internal execution evidence.

requirement: A live WhatsApp session shall have exactly one active worker owner.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: Memory and PostgreSQL lease stores enforce one owner, expiry takeover and stale-fence rejection, and the gateway rejects stale authority before provider send. The production lease acquire/renew lifecycle is not yet wired end-to-end, so operational single ownership is not fully closed.

requirement: Stable worker IPs may be used for isolation; rapid IP rotation or evasion logic is prohibited.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: Governed stable per-session proxy routing exists and active-session proxy changes are rejected. Actual production worker/proxy IP stability and absence of rapid-rotation/evasion behaviour require deployed network evidence.

requirement: A sender’s safe capacity is based on measured evidence and configured headroom, not theoretical batch concurrency.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: Admission uses live healthy-session safe MPM/daily capacity plus configured safety margin/headroom. Those safe-capacity values are supplied through governed session heartbeat state; no evidence yet proves they are derived from measured historical throughput rather than configured inputs.

requirement: The platform shall not accept a hard deadline when measured safe capacity is insufficient without an explicit exception.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: The coordinator refuses campaign start when effective safe capacity cannot meet the hard deadline; admission returns REJECT/HOLD rather than silently accepting an infeasible deadline.

requirement: Unknown outcomes are reconciled before any resend decision.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: Ambiguous submission becomes UNKNOWN and durable gateway idempotency refuses an automatic replay. Reconciliation evidence is required before a resend-safe outcome can be established.

requirement: Contact profile updates cannot silently broaden consent.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: A real PostgreSQL governed profile conflict changes gender from MALE to FEMALE while the existing consent grant remains WITHDRAWN; no new or active consent grant is created.

requirement: Reported age remains as collected; derived estimated age is labelled approximate.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: Imported reported age is retained as supplied with source/recorded-at metadata and SELF_DECLARED_IMPORT evidence. No active derived estimated-age model or approximate-label contract exists, so the full rule is not closed.

requirement: No gender, age, location or interest value shall be inferred without an approved source and policy.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: No active inference engine was found, but there is also no governed approved-source/policy enforcement model for demographic or interest inference. Absence of inference is not sufficient evidence for this policy rule.

requirement: Raw MSISDN values shall not appear in standard logs, URLs or monitoring dimensions.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: Recipient MSISDN is carried in the internal request body rather than the URL. Gateway durability tests prove MSISDN redaction from structured logs and prove Prometheus output for the static /v1/messages route contains no raw recipient MSISDN.

requirement: External organisations do not receive portal access in release one.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: Release-one implementation exposes the internal administration application and internal-user authentication only; no external-organisation portal was found. A dedicated release-surface regression proving no client/self-service portal can be exposed has not yet been added, so this remains conservative.

requirement: All critical overrides require a reason, expiry and audit; high-risk overrides require a second approver.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: Governed overrides/configurations carry reason, effective period, actor history and maker-checker approval. No explicit critical/high-risk override classification or additional second-approver requirement beyond the normal checker was found.

requirement: Every report shall state its metric definitions and provider-status limitations.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: Campaign reports do not yet state complete metric definitions, denominators/formulas and provider-status limitations for every reported measure.

requirement: Suppression is checked again immediately before dispatch.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: The PostgreSQL final eligibility check re-reads active suppressions immediately before submission; a queued recipient becomes ineligible with reason SUPPRESSED and the provider path is not authorised.

requirement: Redis loss must not erase authorised campaign obligations.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: Authorised recipient obligations and durable jobs are PostgreSQL-backed rather than Redis-authoritative. A direct Redis-loss/recovery integration scenario has not yet been executed, so the explicit loss condition remains unclosed.

requirement: A worker crash during submission produces an uncertain state until reconciled; it does not automatically send again.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: A submission crash/ambiguous provider error is recorded as UNKNOWN and durable idempotency blocks automatic re-submission until explicit reconciliation evidence exists.

requirement: Configuration used for consent, segmentation, dispatch and reporting is versioned and retained with the campaign.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: Consent, audience snapshot, routing, provider capability, pacing, capacity and reporting-privacy versions are retained with campaign/execution evidence. The generic configuration catalogue is not yet automatically frozen into every consent, segmentation, dispatch and reporting decision.

requirement: Small demographic report cells are suppressed or grouped according to privacy threshold.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: Governed minimum cohort size is versioned/frozen into report evidence; PostgreSQL report proof suppresses all one-person demographic/geographic cells while leaving a cohort of two visible.

requirement: Campaign evidence and source files are retained or deleted only according to approved retention rules.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: Approved effective-dated retention policies schedule/execute supported import-source, export-object and inbound-content actions with legal-hold/review controls. Full campaign media, provider-event and audit archival/deletion execution is not yet closed.

requirement: A suspended organisation or sender cannot be selected for a new release.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: Suspended organisations fail closed for campaign progression/release, while quarantined sender sessions cannot be restored by heartbeat and contribute zero allocatable capacity.

requirement: All campaign and sender status changes are attributable to a user, service or system policy.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: Campaign transition requests require actor identity, material campaign changes have actor-attributed events, execution transitions have execution events, and sender governance changes are actor-attributed. Ordinary campaign approval-stage CompareAndSwap updates do not persist an equivalent actor-attributed status-history record, so every status change is not yet durably attributable.

requirement: Gateway delivery command shall not contain raw consent or unnecessary demographic data.
acceptance: Payload inspection confirms data minimisation.
notes: The signed gateway delivery command contains only transport authority/routing evidence, recipient address, rendered approved message/media reference and correlation identifiers. A direct payload-inspection test captures the real HTTP command and rejects any field outside that transport set, including consent/suppression/demographic/attribute data.

requirement: Recipient data shall be decrypted only within the minimum authorised boundary required to send.
acceptance: Tracing and access review verify the boundary.
notes: Recipient MSISDN remains encrypted in PostgreSQL until the campaign-worker material loader has loaded approved evidence, allocated a sender and validated the governed route. Decryption occurs immediately before send material construction. Production Compose grants the MSISDN encryption key to campaign-worker but not the OpenWA gateway, and the gateway payload carries only the resulting transport address; production-compose security validation passes.

requirement: Gateway shall reject work for an unowned, paused or incompatible session.
acceptance: Contract test returns canonical rejection.
notes: Control-plane route validation rejects paused/incompatible/stale session evidence and persists fenced authority. PostgreSQL acceptance proves conflicting cross-node authority is rejected/audited without replacing the owner, while the gateway authority check rejects stale/conflicting ownership before provider send.

requirement: Gateway shall return the same accepted result for a repeated idempotency key.
acceptance: Replay test performs no second provider call.
notes: Durable gateway idempotency returns the original accepted provider result for repeated keys without another provider call, including after worker restart. Concurrent identical commands submit once; unresolved/UNKNOWN outcomes fail closed and are never auto-resubmitted.

requirement: Gateway events shall include stable delivery and provider correlation identifiers.
acceptance: Event ingestor matches attempt deterministically.
notes: Gateway events carry stable eventId, control-plane clientReference and providerMessageId. The ingestor resolves deterministically by clientReference first or provider-message lookup when needed, persists provider correlation into delivery evidence, and binds eventId into replay/deduplication; tests prove both correlation modes plus conflicting event-ID replay rejection.

requirement: Gateway capability response shall include message types, engine version and event support.
acceptance: Campaign validation can block unsupported feature.
notes: Gateway capability/identity responses expose engine/adapter version and supported capabilities including message/event support. The control plane freezes the exact provider definition and blocks unsupported message types, engine/adapter versions and capability mismatches before dispatch.

requirement: Service-to-service credentials shall be scoped, rotated and stored outside source code.
acceptance: Secret audit passes.
notes: Service credentials are separated by purpose/service, production wiring uses mounted *_FILE secrets rather than committed values, gateway callback/command/runtime keys support bounded active+previous rotation with distinct strong secrets, and secret-file/production-compose validation passes. The committed-secret audit is also green.

requirement: API schemas shall be backward compatible within a supported major version.
acceptance: Consumer contract tests pass during deployment.
notes: The control API is namespaced under /api/v1, internal gateway events carry explicit schemaVersion 1.0 and current contract/route tests run in CI. However there is no deployment/release gate comparing the current API/schema against a previously supported v1 consumer contract to detect breaking removals or incompatible changes, so backward compatibility within the major version is not fully proven.

requirement: Use an accessible responsive desktop-first interface for internal operations.
acceptance: Core screens pass agreed accessibility audit.
notes: The current Next.js admin shell is desktop-first/responsive with skip navigation, visible focus states, labels and semantic tables, and a fresh production build succeeds. The formal core-screen accessibility audit required by the UI/UX specification has not been run and the frontend programme remains deferred.

requirement: Show environment and classification banners.
acceptance: Production/staging and confidentiality are unmistakable.
notes: The shell displays an environment badge and internal-platform wording, but the badge is currently hardcoded to Development and there is no complete confidentiality/classification banner or verified production/staging differentiation.

requirement: Use masked PII by default with explicit authorised reveal.
acceptance: Default page source contains no plaintext value.
notes: Backend APIs default to masked identifiers and privileged reveal workflows are separately authorised, while the current frontend does not intentionally render raw MSISDNs. No production page-source/back-button acceptance proves plaintext PII is absent across all screens and authorised reveal UX is not implemented.

requirement: Show status, owner, next required action and blocking reasons on every campaign.
acceptance: Operator can determine state without opening logs.
notes: The campaign register displays campaign status and core timing/audience information, and backend campaign-workspace APIs expose richer warnings/next-state evidence. The current campaign UI does not consistently show owner, next required action and blocking reasons on every campaign.

requirement: Provide progressive count waterfall in segment builder.
acceptance: Count/exclusion reasons update and reconcile.
notes: The audience-builder UI has a waterfall-shaped estimate panel for profile matches, consent, suppression and final eligible counts, but it explicitly renders placeholders rather than live reconciled database counts/exclusion reasons. Backend cohort logic exists; the full progressive UX is unfinished.

requirement: Warn clearly when age is approximate or stale.
acceptance: Lagos 18–35 cohort shows age method and staleness.
notes: The current builder supports reported-age filtering but no estimated-age method/staleness model or UI warning exists. The underlying backend estimated-age/staleness requirements are also incomplete.

requirement: Require explicit confirmation for final release, pause, cancel, export and override.
acceptance: Accidental single-click action is prevented.
notes: Backend destructive/release/export paths use permissions, optimistic versions, reasons and MFA/maker-checker controls, preventing an unauthorised single API click from completing sensitive actions. The frontend has no comprehensive explicit confirmation dialogs for release, pause, cancel, export and override.

requirement: Show immutable version identifiers for message, audience, consent review and config.
acceptance: Approval screen identifies exact artefacts.
notes: Backend campaign evidence freezes message/audience/consent/config-related versions, but the current admin campaign screen does not present an approval view identifying the exact immutable artefact versions.

requirement: Show actual sender MSISDN masked and explain logical pool behaviour.
acceptance: No misleading sender-ID representation.
notes: Backend sender APIs mask actual sender MSISDNs, but the current admin-web navigation has no implemented sender page and no UI explanation of logical sender-pool behaviour.

requirement: Provide live operational campaign view with queue, throughput, forecast and incidents.
acceptance: Metrics update within target.
notes: Backend operational APIs provide queue/UNKNOWN/incidents/capacity/forecast evidence, but the current frontend dashboard is not a proven live operational campaign view with target refresh behaviour.

requirement: Use reason codes plus human-readable remediation for failures.
acceptance: Operator can triage without raw stack trace.
notes: Backend errors carry governed reason/detail codes and the UI presents human-readable messages for some forms. There is no complete reason-code-to-remediation catalogue across operational failures, so operators may still need backend context.

requirement: Support saved filters and views without changing authorisation.
acceptance: Personal view persists safely.
notes: No persisted personal saved-filter/view model and no frontend saved-view workflow was found.

requirement: Provide secure export workflow with purpose, approval and expiry.
acceptance: Unapproved bulk export is blocked.
notes: The backend export workflow fully enforces purpose, maker-checker approval, expiry, actor-bound single-use grants, revocation and audit, so unapproved bulk export is blocked. The production frontend reports/export workflow is not implemented, so the UX requirement remains partial.

requirement: Provide keyboard navigation, labelled controls, focus visibility and semantic tables.
acceptance: Accessibility testing passes.
notes: The current UI uses skip navigation, labelled controls, focus-visible styles, semantic tables/fieldsets and keyboard-operable native controls. No formal accessibility/keyboard test suite has yet passed the agreed UI/UX acceptance.

requirement: Prevent dangerous browser caching of sensitive pages.
acceptance: Security headers and back-button behaviour are tested.
notes: Backend sensitive responses apply anti-cache security headers and frontend campaign fetches use no-store. Browser page caching/back-button behaviour across the production admin application has not been tested, so the complete browser-facing acceptance is not closed.

requirement: Expose only reverse-proxy HTTPS endpoints required for the portal/API/webhooks.
acceptance: External port scan matches approved list.
notes: Production Compose publishes no application host ports and places first-party services on an internal private network; the historical reverse-proxy config limits portal/API/health paths. Actual Railway/Hostinger TLS termination and an external port scan against the production endpoints are deferred to infrastructure integration.

requirement: Restrict SSH to approved source IP/VPN and use keys.
acceptance: Unauthorised source cannot connect.
notes: SSH source allowlisting, VPN/key-only access and unauthorised-source connection testing are Hostinger/production-host controls. No deployed production host is available in Task 5, so this remains an explicit infrastructure gate.

requirement: Block public PostgreSQL and Redis access.
acceptance: External scan and firewall rules verify.
notes: The first-party production stack uses an internal network and does not publish PostgreSQL or Redis ports; the agreed Railway architecture also keeps managed data services private. The acceptance requires real production firewall/external-scan evidence, which is deferred.

requirement: Allow gateway/control communication only between approved node identities.
acceptance: Firewall/service-auth test passes.
notes: Control/gateway commands, callbacks and runtime reports are signed, replay-resistant and bound to governed node identities; production Compose isolates service traffic. Cross-provider firewall/static-egress and optional mTLS evidence require the Railway/Hostinger deployment.

requirement: Use DNS and certificates that can move to another provider.
acceptance: Migration test/plan has no hardcoded IP dependency.
notes: Service/object-store/gateway endpoints are parameterised by DNS/service URL rather than hardcoded production IPs, preserving provider portability. A real DNS/certificate move and migration exercise has not yet been performed.

requirement: Synchronise time securely across nodes.
acceptance: Clock drift stays within event/signature tolerance.
notes: Signed command/callback/runtime contracts enforce bounded timestamp skew, but secure NTP/time-synchronisation is a node/hosting control. Clock-drift evidence across Railway and Hostinger nodes requires the production infrastructure phase.

requirement: Record node inventory, OS, IP, role and deployed version.
acceptance: Operations CMDB/view is complete.
notes: Gateway runtime inventory persists governed node ID, pool/provider/engine, adapter/gateway/worker/config versions, internal URL, boot ID, capabilities, state, capacity and resource telemetry. It does not provide a complete CMDB record of host OS, public/private IP and infrastructure role for every production node.

requirement: Apply OS and container security updates through controlled maintenance.
acceptance: Patch evidence and rollback procedure exist.
notes: Application maintenance/drain controls can stop unsafe new work and gracefully drain active gateway operations, but OS/container patch execution evidence and a tested host rollback procedure require deployed Railway/Hostinger environments.

requirement: Separate production, staging and monitoring credentials.
acceptance: Secret/access review passes.
notes: Production services use distinct mounted secret files and scoped database identities, and active/smoke development gateway identities are separated. A production/staging/monitoring credential inventory and access review across the deployed providers has not yet been executed.

requirement: Implement disk, memory, CPU, inode, process/PID and network alerts.
acceptance: Failure simulation triggers alert.
notes: Runtime telemetry now covers CPU, memory, disk bytes, inode counts, PID/uptime, file descriptors and network RX/TX/interface count, and governed operational alerts cover node/session health and backlog. Alert policies do not yet expose dedicated disk/inode/PID/network threshold metrics and no production failure simulation has demonstrated notification delivery.

requirement: Perform scheduled PostgreSQL full backups and continuous/incremental WAL archiving.
acceptance: Backup catalogue shows successful recoverable chain.
notes: Scheduled PostgreSQL full backup/PITR/WAL archiving is a Railway production data-plane control. No production backup catalogue or recoverable chain exists yet; this is intentionally deferred to infrastructure integration.

requirement: Encrypt backups before or during transfer to an independent target.
acceptance: Stored backup is unreadable without approved key.
notes: Independent-target backup encryption and key-controlled unreadability require the production backup destination/key-management design and live evidence; no such deployed backup exists in Task 5.

requirement: Keep backup credentials separate from primary database credentials.
acceptance: Access review passes.
notes: Application database credentials are scoped and secret-file mounted, but a distinct production backup identity/credential set does not exist until the backup service is provisioned and access-reviewed.

requirement: Back up object metadata and evidence/media according to retention.
acceptance: Recovery restores object and checksum.
notes: PostgreSQL retains object ownership/checksum/metadata while object bytes reside in private S3-compatible storage, but no independent object/evidence backup and restore exercise has yet restored bytes plus checksum under retention policy.

requirement: Back up configuration, infrastructure code and deployment manifests through private repository.
acceptance: Environment can be recreated.
notes: Application deployment manifests, Dockerfiles and configuration are version-controlled in this repository and can reproduce the application topology. The required private hosted-repository assurance and a clean environment recreation exercise are not yet evidenced.

requirement: Do not rely solely on Hostinger weekly whole-VPS backup.
acceptance: Database-level recovery evidence exists.
notes: The agreed production direction requires database-level recovery independent of VPS snapshots, but no production Railway database backup/restore evidence exists yet. Hostinger whole-VPS backup will not be accepted as the sole recovery mechanism.

requirement: Test restoration at least monthly during initial production maturity.
acceptance: Signed restore-test report exists.
notes: Monthly production restore testing cannot begin before the production backup chain exists. No signed restore-test report exists yet.

requirement: Validate restored data integrity, row counts, keys and application compatibility.
acceptance: Automated validation passes.
notes: General release/data integrity checks exist, but no automated post-restore validation currently proves restored row counts, cryptographic keys/object checksums and application compatibility because no production restore target is available yet.

requirement: Document and test replica promotion or recovery-target activation.
acceptance: Exercise meets RTO or records remediation.
notes: Replica promotion or recovery-target activation is provider/infrastructure work and has not been exercised against Railway/production PostgreSQL. RTO evidence is therefore unavailable.

requirement: Protect backups against ordinary application deletion and ransomware.
acceptance: Immutability/versioning policy is evidenced.
notes: Backup immutability/versioning and ransomware separation depend on the selected independent backup target. No deployed policy/evidence exists yet.

requirement: An authorised internal user can create an organisation and record a consent review with evidence, restrictions and expiry.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: Organisation and consent-review permissions, evidence, restrictions, expiry and independent review are individually enforced. No single authorised-user workflow test composes organisation creation through a recorded approved consent review.

requirement: The system securely imports and reconciles a large contact file, preserving source and validation reasons.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: Secure protected staging, source lineage, validation issues and reconciliation are tested, including streaming XLSX parsing. No single genuinely large contact-file acceptance run composes secure upload, validation, merge and reconciliation end to end.

requirement: The platform stores MSISDN encrypted, deduplicates using HMAC and masks it in UI/logs.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: PostgreSQL encryption/HMAC dedup, API masking and log/metric redaction are directly evidenced. Production frontend/UI masking remains deferred.

requirement: The segment builder creates a Lagos age 18–35 cohort using the configured self-declared-age policy.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: The cohort compiler directly builds NG/Lagos reported-age 18-35 selection with consent eligibility. The configured self-declared-age policy/staleness model required by the acceptance sentence is not fully implemented.

requirement: The final eligible count applies organisation/purpose/channel consent, expiry, suppression and frequency caps.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: Final eligibility directly enforces active matching organisation/purpose/channel consent, expiry/withdrawal, suppression, contact state and governed frequency-cap policy at release/dispatch boundaries.

requirement: The system creates an immutable audience snapshot and preserves policy/configuration versions.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: PostgreSQL rejects audience-snapshot mutation/deletion, and snapshot/materialisation evidence carries definition, consent-policy and configuration versions used for the campaign.

requirement: A campaign message and media are versioned, scanned, tested and approved through maker-checker.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: Message/media versioning, malware-clean trusted assets, controlled test sends and maker-checker approvals are individually tested. No single message+media workflow composes scan, test send and final maker-checker approval end to end.

requirement: Campaign entitlement prevents excess or duplicate recipients.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: PostgreSQL release rejects entitlement overflow transactionally with zero recipient/outbox rows; replay keeps exactly one recipient/outbox, and entitlement cannot be reused by another campaign.

requirement: Recipient records/outbox are created atomically and queue can be rebuilt.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: Recipient ledger and transactional outbox are created atomically and an expired publisher claim is recoverable. A queue job lost after its outbox row is already PUBLISHED cannot yet be reconstructed automatically.

requirement: A gateway worker sends only for sessions it exclusively owns and honours idempotency.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: Exclusive session authority/fencing and send idempotency are directly tested. Production lease acquisition, renewal and controlled ownership handover are not yet proven end to end across the live worker lifecycle.

requirement: Worker and queue failure tests do not silently lose obligations or automatically duplicate uncertain sends.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: Crash reclaim, job deduplication, late eligibility suppression and UNKNOWN/no-unsafe-resend behavior are tested. The published-outbox/lost-queue reconstruction gap can still strand an obligation, so silent-loss resilience is not fully closed.

requirement: Campaign metrics accurately distinguish gateway accepted, sent, delivered, read, failed and unknown.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: Delivery ledger states distinguish gateway accepted, sent, delivered, read, failed and UNKNOWN, but campaign metrics currently fold GATEWAY_ACCEPTED together with SUBMITTING into submitted_total rather than exposing gateway-accepted separately.

requirement: An opt-out after snapshot prevents subsequent dispatch and appears in reporting.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: A post-snapshot withdrawal/suppression prevents later dispatch. Reports expose optOuts from opt_out_total, but no production writer updates opt_out_total, so the same opt-out is not guaranteed to appear in reporting.

requirement: A five-million-recipient synthetic campaign ledger can be created, resumed, queried and reported within accepted performance.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: The synthetic five-million release test proves bounded 5,000-recipient batches and bounded sharding, but it does not create/resume/query/report a real persisted five-million-recipient ledger or measure the full acceptance workload.

requirement: A ten-million-contact synthetic repository supports required cohort queries within accepted performance.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: Ten-million synthetic query benchmarking exists outside the repo and the production schema/compiler has high-volume indexes and bounded materialisation. The complete governed cohort path has not been benchmarked against ten million canonical contacts within accepted performance.

requirement: The Hostinger pilot environment is reproducible, monitored, backed up and successfully restored.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: Production deployment/monitoring/backup design exists, but the acceptance truth requires a real Hostinger pilot plus successful backup/restore exercise. That external environment evidence does not yet exist.

requirement: Security testing shows role isolation, MFA, safe uploads, no PII logs and protected exports.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: Fresh security suites prove role/permission isolation, MFA/step-up, malware-safe uploads, PII/secret log redaction and permission+MFA+maker-checker protection for exports.

requirement: Audit evidence reconstructs the full path from consent review through final report.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: Append-only/audited evidence exists at consent, audience/import, campaign, execution/delivery and reporting stages, but there is no single acceptance test that reconstructs one complete chain from consent review through final report.

requirement: The private repository retains MIT attribution, blocks direct main changes and does not auto-merge upstream.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: MIT attribution is retained and CI runs on pull requests/pushes; no upstream auto-merge workflow was found. This checkout origin is a local bundle, so hosted private-repository branch protection/direct-main blocking cannot be verified here.

requirement: Operational owners approve runbooks, emergency stop, incident response and capacity representation.
acceptance: See acceptance criteria and linked tests.
notes: Emergency/governance, incident/operations and capacity-representation controls exist in software, but formal operational-owner approval of runbooks, emergency stop and incident/capacity procedures remains an external readiness gate.
